questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to crystal field theory, the correct order of ligands with respect to their decreasing order of field strength is
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the arrangement of ligands in the increasing order of their crystal field splitting energy (CFSE) or field strength is:

$\text{I}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{SCN}^- < \text{Cl}^- < \text{S}^{2-} < \text{F}^- < \text{OH}^- < \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} < \text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{NCS}^- < \text{edta}^{4-} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{en} < \text{CN}^- < \text{CO}$

From the given ligands, the decreasing order of field strength is:

$\text{CO} > \text{NH}_3 > \text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{Cl}^-$

Answer: $\text{CO}>\text{NH}_3>\text{H}_2\text{O}>\text{Cl}^-$

questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Complex/ion)List II (Shape/geometry)
A. $[\text{Pt}(\text{Cl}_2)(\text{NH}_3)_2]$I. Octahedral
B. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$II. Trigonal bipyramidal
C. $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$III. Square planar
D. $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$IV. Tetrahedral

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
For $[\text{Pt}(\text{Cl}_2)(\text{NH}_3)_2]$, Pt is in $+2$ oxidation state. Pt(II) complexes are generally square planar with $dsp^2$ hybridization.

For $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$, Co is in $+3$ oxidation state. With a coordination number of 6, it forms an octahedral geometry.

For $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, Ni is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^8$). Since $\text{Cl}^-$ is a weak field ligand, no pairing of electrons occurs, resulting in $sp^3$ hybridization and a tetrahedral geometry.

For $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$, Fe is in $0$ oxidation state. With a coordination number of 5, it forms a trigonal bipyramidal geometry with $dsp^3$ hybridization.

Therefore, the correct matching is A $\rightarrow$ III, B $\rightarrow$ I, C $\rightarrow$ IV, D $\rightarrow$ II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.q: The formula of tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride is
questions.solution:
The complex name is tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride.

The central metal ion is cobalt(III), which means $\text{Co}$ is in the $+3$ oxidation state.

The ligands inside the coordination sphere are four ammine ($\text{NH}_3$) molecules which are neutral, one aqua ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) molecule which is neutral, and one chlorido ($\text{Cl}^-$) ion which has a $-1$ charge.

The coordination sphere is $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})\text{Cl}]$.

The charge on the complex ion is calculated as $+3 + 4(0) + 0 + (-1) = +2$.

To balance the $+2$ charge of the complex ion, two chloride ($\text{Cl}^-$) counter ions are required outside the coordination sphere.

Thus, the formula of the complex is $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$.

Answer: $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$

questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Complex)List II (Type of isomerism)
A. $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$I. Optical
B. $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$II. Solvate
C. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{NO}_2]\text{Cl}_2$III. Geometrical
D. $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]\text{Cl}_3$IV. Linkage

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
A. $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ is a square planar complex of the type $MA_2B_2$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms).

B. $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$ is an octahedral complex with three symmetrical bidentate ligands. It lacks a plane of symmetry and exhibits optical isomerism.

C. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{NO}_2]\text{Cl}_2$ contains the ambidentate ligand $\text{NO}_2^-$, which can coordinate through either the nitrogen or oxygen atom. It exhibits linkage isomerism.

D. $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]\text{Cl}_3$ can exchange water molecules with chloride ions to form different hydrate isomers. It exhibits solvate isomerism.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : $[\text{Fe(ox)}_3]^{3-}$ is chiral.
Statement-II : $\textit{trans}-[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{ox})_2]^-$ is chiral.
(Given : oxH$_2$ = HOOC$-$COOH)
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement-I: $[\text{Fe(ox)}_3]^{3-}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[M(AA)_3]$. It lacks any plane of symmetry or center of inversion. Hence, it is optically active and chiral. Statement-I is correct.

Statement-II: $\textit{trans}-[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{ox})_2]^-$ is an octahedral complex of the type $\textit{trans}-[M(AA)_2a_2]$. In the trans isomer, the two identical monodentate ligands are placed opposite to each other. This geometry possesses a plane of symmetry passing through the metal and the bidentate ligands, as well as a center of inversion. Hence, it is optically inactive and achiral. Statement-II is incorrect.

Therefore, Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.

(Given : py = pyridine and en = H$_2$N$-$CH$_2-$CH$_2-$NH$_2$)
questions.solution:

$[\text{Cr(py)}_3(\text{Cl})_3]$ is of the type $[MA_3B_3]$, which shows facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism.

$[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ is of the type $[MA_6]$, which does not show geometrical isomerism.

$[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2]^{3+}$ is of the type $[MA_4B_2]$, which shows cis and trans isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Among the species given below, the spin-only magnetic moment is highest for
(Given : Atomic number of Ti $=22$, Mn $=25$, Fe $=26$ and Co $=27$)
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons. We determine $n$ for each complex:

For $[\text{Ti(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$:
Ti is in $+3$ oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Ti$^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^1$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 1$.
$\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3}$ BM.

For $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$:
Mn is in $+3$ oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Mn$^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$.
Since CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, pairing of electrons takes place. The configuration in the octahedral field is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^0$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 2$.
$\mu = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8}$ BM.

For $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$:
Fe is in $+3$ oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Fe$^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5$.
CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing. The configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 1$.
$\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3}$ BM.

For $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$:
Co is in $+3$ oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Co$^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.
NH$_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for Co$^{3+}$, causing complete pairing. The configuration is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 0$.
$\mu = 0$ BM.

Comparing the values, $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ has the highest number of unpaired electrons ($n=2$) and thus the highest spin-only magnetic moment.

Answer: $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Both $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ and $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_6\right]^{3-}$ complexes are octahedral but differ in their magnetic behaviour.
Statement II: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ is diamagnetic whereas $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_6\right]^{3-}$ is paramagnetic.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}, \mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ ion is having $3 \mathrm{~d}^6$ configuration. Electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ :
In presence of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ ligand, pairing of electrons takes place and it becomes diamagnetic complex ion. In presence of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ ligand :
$\therefore \quad\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ is octahedral with $\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridisation and it is diamagnetic in nature. In case of $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_6\right]^{3-}$, Co is in +3 oxidation state and it is having $3 \mathrm{~d}^6$ configuration. In presence of weak field $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ligand, pairing does not take place. In presence of $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ligands :
$\therefore$ In $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_6\right]^{3-}, \mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ is $\mathrm{sp}^3 \mathrm{~d}^2$ hybridised with four unpaired electrons, so it is paramagnetic in nature.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ is a homoleptic complex whereas $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$is a heteroleptic complex.
Statement II : Complex $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ has only one kind of ligands but $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$has more than one kind of ligands.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ is a homoleptic complex as only one type of ligands $\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)$ is coordinated with $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ ion. While $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$is a heteroleptic complex in which $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ ion is ligated with more than one type of ligands, i.e., $\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A 1:3 electrolyte in an aqueous solution is
questions.solution:
A 1:3 electrolyte dissociates in an aqueous solution to give one cation and three anions, or vice versa, producing a total of four ions per formula unit.

$[\text{Co(NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$ is a neutral complex and does not dissociate into ions. It is a non-electrolyte.

$[\text{CoCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Cl} \rightarrow [\text{CoCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{+} + \text{Cl}^{-}$ (1:1 electrolyte)

$[\text{CoCl(NH}_3)_5]\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow [\text{CoCl(NH}_3)_5]^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^{-}$ (1:2 electrolyte)

$[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3 \rightarrow [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^{-}$ (1:3 electrolyte)

Thus, $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$ is a 1:3 electrolyte.

Answer: $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is an ambidentate ligand ?
questions.solution:
An ambidentate ligand is a unidentate ligand that has more than one donor atom but coordinates to the central metal atom or ion through only one donor atom at a time.

Thiocyanate ion ($SCN^{-}$ or $NCS^{-}$) has two donor atoms, sulfur ($S$) and nitrogen ($N$). It can bind to the metal through either the sulfur atom (thiocyanato) or the nitrogen atom (isothiocyanato). Thus, it is an ambidentate ligand.

Ethane-$1,2$-diamine is a bidentate ligand.

Ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion is a hexadentate ligand.

Oxalate is a bidentate ligand.

Answer: Thiocyanate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which complex compound is most stable?
questions.solution:
Chelating ligands in general form more stable complexes than their monodentate analogs. When a chelating ligand binds to a metal ion, it forms a ring structure with the metal ion at the center. This ring structure increases the stability of the complex because it restricts the movement of the metal ion and prevents it from interacting with other molecules or ions. In addition, the chelating ligand can donate multiple electron pairs to the metal ion, which increases the strength of the metal-ligand bond and further stabilizes the complex.

∴ The most stable complex is $\left[{CoCl}_{2}{\left(en\right)}_{2}\right]{NO}_{3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Jahn-Teller effect is not observed in high spin complexes of
questions.solution: Jahn Teller effect (JTE) explains the axial distortion in perfect octahedral geometry. It is present in ${d}^{4}$ high spin, ${d}^{7}$ low spin and ${d}^{9}$ configuration, which have an odd number of electrons in a ${e}_{g}$ set. A weak Jahn Teller effect is also present in ${d}^{7}$ high spin complex, which has an odd number of electrons in the set. Therefore, the Jahn Teller effect is not observed in high spin complexes of ${d}^{8}$ orbital.

questions.q: Which of the following has the longest $C - O$ bond length? (Free $C - O$ bond length in $CO$ is $1 . 128\overset{o}{A}$).
questions.solution:
Metal carbon bond in metal carbonyls possess both $\sigma$ and $\pi$ character. $\text{M} - \text{C}\pi$ bond is formed by donation of a pair of electrons from filled orbital of metal into vacant antibonding $\pi$ orbital of $\text{CO}$ . $\text{CO}$ bond length increases if M has more tendency to donate lone pair.

Tendency to donate lone pair is ${Fe}^{2 -} > {Co}^{−} > Ni > {Mn}^{+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is an outer orbital complex and exhibits paramagnetic behaviour?
questions.solution:
Outer orbital complex utilises nd orbitals for bonding and exhibit paramagnetic behaviour, only if there present unpaired electrons.
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{(a) } \operatorname{In}\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{2+}: \\
& \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^8 4 s^0
\end{aligned}$


So, this is an outer orbital complex having paramagnetic character.
(b) In $\left[\mathrm{Zn}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ :
$\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^{10}$

Thus, it is also an outer orbital complex but it is diamagnetic as all the electrons are paired.
$\begin{gathered}
\text{(c) } \operatorname{In}\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+} \\
\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^3 \\
{\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}=}
\end{gathered}$

Because of the involvement of $(n-1) d$, i.e., $3 d$ orbital in hybridisation, it is an inner orbital complex. Its nature is paramagnetic because of the presence of three unpaired electrons.
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{(d) } \operatorname{In}\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+} \text{ : } \\
& \mathrm{Co}^{3+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^6
\end{aligned}$

As all the electrons are paired, it is a diamagnetic complex.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Low spin complex of $d^6$-cation in an octahedral field will have the following energy
$\left(\Delta_o=\right.$ crystal field splitting energy in an octahedral field, $P=$ electron pairing energy)
questions.solution:
\(\text{C.F.S.E. }=(-0.4 x+0.6 y) \Delta_o+z P\)
where \(\mathrm{x}=\) number of electrons occupying \(\mathrm{t}_{2 g}\) orbital
\(y=\) number of electrons occupying \(e_g\) orbital
\(z=\) number of pairs of electrons
For low spin \(\mathrm{d}^6\) complex electronic configuration
$\begin{aligned}
& =t_{2 g}^6 e_g^0 \text{$ or $} t_{2 g}^{2,2,2} e_g^0 \\
& \therefore \quad x=6, y=0, z=3 \\
& \text{ C.F.S.E. }=(-0.4 \times 6+0 \times 0.6) \Delta_o+3 P \\
& =\frac{-12}{5} \Delta_o+3 P
\end{aligned}\)$

questions.q: Which of the following carbonyls will have the strongest $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Crystal field stabilization energy for high spin $\mathrm{d}^4$ octahedral complex is
questions.solution:
Key Idea:- In case of high spin complex, $\Delta_0$ is small. Thus, the energy required to pair up the fourth electron with the electrons of lower energy d-orbitals would be higher than that required to place the electrons in the higher d-orbital. Thus, pairing does not occur. For high spin $\mathrm{d}^4$ octahedral complex,
$\therefore$ Crystal field stabilisation energy $\begin{aligned}$& =(-3 $\times$0.4+1 $\times$0.6) \Delta_{{}^{\circ}} \\ & =(-1.2+0.6) \Delta_0 \\ & =-0.6 \Delta_0 \end{aligned}

Which of the following does not show optical isomerism?
(en = ethylenediamine)
questions.solution:
Optical isomerism is exhibited by only those complexes in which elements of symmetry are absent. Octahedral complexes of the types $\left[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{aa})_3\right],\left[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{aa}) \mathrm{x}_2, \mathrm{y}_2\right]$ and $\left[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{aa})_2 \mathrm{x}_2\right]$ have absence of elements of symmetry, thus exhibit optical isomerism. Here, $a a$ represents bidentate ligand, $x$ or $y$ represents monodentate ligand and $M$ represents central metal ion.
Hence, $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{Cl}_3\right]^0$ due to presence of symmetry elements does not exhibit optical isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In which of the following coordination entities the magnitude of $\Delta_o$ (CFSE in octahedral field) will be maximum?
(Atomic number $\mathrm{Co}=27$ )
questions.solution:
Key Idea: The magnitude of $\Delta_{\propto \mathrm{c} t}$ (the orbital splitting energy) is decided by the nature of ligand Strong field ligand has highest $\Delta_{\text{oct }}$. The increasing field strength is as
$\mathrm{I}^{-} < \mathrm{Br}^{-} < \mathrm{Cl}^{-} < \mathrm{F}^{-} < \mathrm{OH}^{-} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} < \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4^{2-} < \mathrm{NH}_3 < \mathrm{en} < \mathrm{NO}_2^{-} < \mathrm{CN}^{-}
The \mathrm{CN}^{-}$is the strongest ligand among these, hence the magnitude of $\Delta_{\text{oct }}$ will be maximum in $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$.


Note : The magnitude of $\Delta_{\text{oct }}$ is also decided by oxidation state of the metal ion. Thus, greater the ionic charge on the central metal ion, the greater the value of $\Delta_{\text{oct }}$. But here the oxidatinon state of Co metal ion is same in all complexes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following complexes exhibits the highest paramagnetic behaviour?
where gly = glycine, en = ethylenediamine and bpy = bipyridyl moities
(At no: $\mathrm{Ti}=22, \mathrm{~V}=23, \mathrm{Fe}=26, \mathrm{Co}=27$ )
questions.solution:
Key Idea : Greater is the number of unpaired electrons, larger is the paramagnetism.
$\begin{aligned}
& {\left[\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{gly})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{+}} \\
& \mathrm{V}_{23}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^3
\end{aligned}$
Oxidation state of $\mathrm{V}$ in $\left[\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{gly})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{+}$ is
$\begin{gathered}
x+(-1) \times 2+(-1) \times 2+(0) \times 2=+1 \\
x=+5 \\
\mathrm{~V}^{5+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^0
\end{gathered}$
(No unpaired electron in option (A))
So, option (B),
$\begin{aligned}
& {\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\text{ en) }(\text{ bpy })\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{2+}\right.} \\
& \mathrm{Fe}_{26}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^6
\end{aligned}$
Oxidation state of $\mathrm{Fe}$ in $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{en}) \text{ (bpy) }\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{2+}$ is
$\begin{gathered}
x+(0)+(0)+(0) \times 2=+2 \\
x=+2 \\
\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^6
\end{gathered}$
But en, bpy and $\mathrm{NH}_3$ all are strong field ligands so pairing occurs, thus no unpaired electrons.
So, option (C),
$\begin{gathered}
{\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OX})_2(\mathrm{OH}]_2\right]^{-}} \\
\mathrm{Co}_{27}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^7
\end{gathered}$
Oxidation state of $\mathrm{Co}$ in $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OX})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\right]^{-}$is
$x+(-2) \times 2+(-1) \times 2=-1$
$\begin{aligned}
& x-6=-1 \\
& x=+5 \\
& \mathrm{Co}^{5+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^4 \\
& \text{(4 paired electrons)} \\
& \text{Now, option (D),} \\
& {\left[\mathrm{Ti}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}} \\
& \mathrm{Ti}_{22}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^2
\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{Ti}_{22}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^2$
Oxidation state of Ti in $\left[\mathrm{Ti}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ is +3, thus it contains 1 unpaired electron.
Hence, $\quad\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OX})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\right]^{-}$has highest paramagnetic behaviour.

Oxidation state of $\mathrm{Co}$ in $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OX})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\right]^{-}$is
$x+(-2) \times 2+(-1) \times 2=-1$
$\begin{aligned}
& x-6=-1 \\
& x=+5 \\
& \mathrm{Co}^{5+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^4 \\
& \text{(4 paired electrons)} \\
& \text{Now, option (D),} \\
& {\left[\mathrm{Ti}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}} \\
& \mathrm{Ti}_{22}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^2
\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{Ti}_{22}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 4 s^2, 3 d^2$
Oxidation state of Ti in $\left[\mathrm{Ti}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ is +3, thus it contains 1 unpaired electron.
Hence, $\quad\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{OX})_2(\mathrm{OH})_2\right]^{-}$has highest paramagnetic behaviour.

options: it can accept electrons from metal species
it form high spin complexes with metal species
questions.solution:
Cyanide ion is strong field ligand because it is a pseudohalide ion. Pseudohalide ions are stronger coordinating ligand \& they have the ability to form $\sigma$ bond (from the pseudohalide to the metal) and $\pi$ bond (from the metal to pseudohalide).
Related Theory
A pseudohalide is an anion which has similar properties to a halogen, but not a real halogen. Pseudohalogens are polyatomic analogues of halogens, or also called 'fake' halogens, whose properties resemble that of true halogens.

questions.q:
Which of the following complex ions is expected to absorb visible light ?
(At. no. $\mathrm{Zn}=30, \mathrm{Sc}=21, \mathrm{Ti}=22, \mathrm{Cr}=24$ )
questions.solution:
Key Idea Only those transition metal complexes are expected to absorb visible light, in which d-subshell is incomplete (ie, has unpaired electron) and excitation of electron from a lower energy arbital to higher energy orbital is possible. (a) In $\left[\mathrm{Sc}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_3\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_3\right]^{3+}, \mathrm{Sc}$ is present as $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$. $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]3 \mathrm{ d}^0, 4 \mathrm{ s}^0 Since,$ in $this complex excitation of electron is not possible, it will not absorb visible light. (b) In \left[\mathrm{Ti}(\mathrm{en})_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{4+}, \mathrm{Ti}$ is present as $\mathrm{Ti}^{4+}$. $\mathrm{Ti}^{4+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]3 \mathrm{ d}^0, 4 \mathrm{ s}^0 Hence, it will not absorb visible light. (c)$ In $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}, \mathrm{Cr}$ is present as $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$. $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]3 \mathrm{ d}^3, 4 \mathrm{ s}^0 $\\ Since, this complex has three unpaired electrons, excitation of $electrons is possible and thus, it is expected that this complex will absorb visible light. (d) In \left[\mathrm{Zn}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{2+}, \mathrm{Zn}$ is present as $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$. $\begin{gathered}\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]3 \mathrm{ d}^{10},4 \mathrm{ s}^0 \\ {\left[\mathrm{Zn}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}$\right)_6\right]^{2+}=[$\mathrm{Ar}]$3 d^{10}} \end{gathered}
Hence, this complex will not absorb visible light.

The oxidation number of $\mathrm{Fe}$ in the complex, $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_5 \mathrm{NO}\right] \mathrm{SO}_4$ is $+1$ [$\mathrm{NO}$ has $+1$ charge]
$\mathrm{Fe}^{+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^6 4 s^1 \mathrm{NO}^{+}$ causes pairing of 4 s electron inside.
Thus, the configuration is $3 d^7$ and number of unpaired electrons $=3$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion $A$ and the other is labelled as Reason $R .$

Assertion A: The spin only magnetic moment value for ${\left[Fe ( CN{)}_{6}\right]}^{3 -}$ is $1 . 74BM,$ whereas for [Fe(H2O)6]${\left[Fe{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{3 +}$ is $5 . 92BM .$

Reason B: In both complexes, $Fe$ is present in $+ 3$ oxidation state.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are true but $R$ is $NOT$ the correct explanation of $A$
Both $A$ and $R$ are true and$R$ is the correct explanation of $A$
questions.solution:
$[ Fe ( {H}_{2}O{)}_{6}{]}^{3 +}$ has magnetic moment value of $5 . 92BM$ because ${H}_{2}O$  is a weak ligand and pairing will not occur. It involves ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$ hybridisation with five unpaired electrons (because magnetic moment is equal to $5 . 92BM$) and outer orbital complex is formed. Magnetic moment can be calculated by the formula ${\mu}_{m} = \sqrt{n ( n + 2 )}$ $BM$ where, ${\mu}_{m} =$magnetic moment, $n =$number of unpaired electron(s).

${\mu}_{m} = 1 . 74BM, n = 1$
${\mu}_{m} = 5 . 92BM, n = 5$

In $[ Fe ( CN{)}_{6}{]}^{3 –}$complex ${CN}^{-}$ is stronger ligand than ${H}_{2}O$ according to spectrochemical series.  Hence, four electrons will pair itself. It involves ${d}^{2}{sp}^{3}$hybridisation with one unpaired electron and inner orbital complex is formed and has a value of only $1 . 74BM$.

In Bothe the complexes the oxidation state of iron is +3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The crystal filed theory is successful in explaining which of the following?

I. Ligands as point charges;

II. Formation and structures of complexes.

III. colour;

IV. Magnetic properties:

V . covalent character of metal-ligand bonding.
questions.solution: The crystal field theory (CFT) is an electrostatic model which considers the metal-ligand bond to be ionic arising purely from electrostatic interactions between the metal ion and the ligand. Ligands are treated as point charges in case of anions or point dipoles in case of neutral molecules. The colour in the coordination compounds can be readily explained in terms of the crystal field theory. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following are the example of double salt?

(A) ${FeSO}_{4} \cdot {\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{2}{SO}_{4} \cdot 6{H}_{2}O$

(B) ${CuSO}_{4} \cdot 4{NH}_{3} \cdot {H}_{2}O$

(C) ${K}_{2}{SO}_{4} \cdot {Al}_{2}{\left({SO}_{4}\right)}_{3} \cdot 24{H}_{2}O$

(D) $Fe ( CN{)}_{2} \cdot 4KCN$

Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution:
A double salt is a salt that contains two or more different cations or anions.

(A) ${FeSO}_{4} + {\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{2}{SO}_{4} + 6{H}_{2}O \to {FeSO}_{4} \cdot {\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{2}{SO}_{4} \cdot 6{H}_{2}O$(Mohr's salt)

Mohr’s salt called double salt which contains more than one simple salt. It undergoes complete dissociation in aqueous solutions.

(B) ${CuSO}_{4} \cdot 4{NH}_{3} \cdot {H}_{2}O$

Ammonia solution in water gives a blue precipitate when it combines with a solution of copper salt. The pale blue precipitate of copper hydroxide dissolves in excess of ammonium hydroxide forming tetraamine copper[II] sulphate, an azure blue (deep blue) soluble complex salt.

(C) ${K}_{2}{SO}_{4} \cdot {Al}_{2}{\left({SO}_{4}\right)}_{3} \cdot 24{H}_{2}O$ (Potash alum)

It is a double salt. Basically, it is comprised of two simple salts potassium sulphate and aluminium sulphate. Potash alum will not be wet in its solid form because the water of crystallisation is not free.

(D) $Fe ( CN{)}_{2} \cdot 4KCN$

It is complex salt. It does not dissociate completely into individual ions.

So, the correct answer is A and C only.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
If ${Ni}^{2 +}$ is replaced by ${Pt}^{2 +}$ in the complex ${\left[{NiCl}_{2}{Br}_{2}\right]}^{2 -}$, which of the following properties are expected to get changed?
A. Geometry
B. Geometrical isomerism
C. Optical isomerism
D. Magnetic properties
questions.solution:
When${Ni}^{2 +}$ is replaced by${Pt}^{2 +}$ in the complex ${\left[{NiCl}_{2}{Br}_{2}\right]}^{2 -}$, the following properties are expected to be changed:

A. Geometry: Since ${Pt}^{2 +}$ and${Ni}^{2 +}$ have different coordination preferences and atomic sizes, the replacement is likely to result in a change in the geometry of the complex. That is it changes to square planar.

B. Geometrical isomerism: If the replacement of ${Ni}^{2 +}$ with ${Pt}^{2 +}$ leads to a change in the ligand arrangement, it can result in the generation of cis and trans isomers.

C. Magnetic properties: ${\left[{PtCl}_{2}{Br}_{2}\right]}^{2 -}$ is diamagnetic.

Both the complex species are optically inactive.

$( II )$ $Ni\left(II\right)$ complex can very rarely be of low spin.

questions.solution:
With weak field ligands Mn(II) will be of high spin and with strong field ligands it will be of low spin. Ni(II) tetrahedral complexes will be genrally of high spin due to ${sp}^{3}$ hybridisation. It can very rarely be of low spin when ligand field is very strong.

$\left(II\right)$ ${\left[{RuCl}_{6}\right]}^{2 -}$ $\left(Q\right)$ $\mu\left(spin - only\right) = 4 . 9BM$
$\left(III\right)$ ${\left[Cr{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ $\left(R\right)$ low spin complex ion
$\left(IV\right)$ ${\left[Fe{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ $\left(S\right)$ metal ion in $4 +$ oxidation state
    $\left(T\right)$ ${d}^{4}$ species

$\left(I\right){\left[Cr{\left(CN\right)}_{6}\right]}^{4 -}$

${Cr}^{2} = \left[Ar\right]3{d}^{4}4{s}^{0}$

$\left(II\right){\left[{RuCl}_{6}\right]}^{2 -}$

Low spin complex as Ru belongs to 4d series, as elements belonging to 4d and 5d series forms low spin complexes even with weak field ligand.

${Ru}^{+ 4} = \left[Kr\right]4{d}^{4}5{s}^{0}$

${t}_{2g}$ set contains $4$ electrons.

$\left(III\right){\left[Cr{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$

${Cr}^{+ 2} = \left[Ar\right]3{d}^{4}4{s}^{0}$

Its configuration is ${t}_{2g}^{3}{e}_{g}^{1}$

It has $4$ unpaired ${e}^{-}$ as ${H}_{2}O$ is weak field ligand.

So, its Magnetic moment, $\mu = 4 . 9B . M$

$\left(IV\right){\left[Fe\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]}^{2 +}$

${Fe}^{2 +} = \left[Ar\right]3{d}^{6}4{s}^{0}$

$= {t}_{2g}^{4}{e}_{g}^{2}$

It has $4$ unpaired ${e}^{-}$, its Magnetic moment, $\mu = 4 . 9B . M .

$

(D) ${\left[Fe{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ IV ${d}^{2}{sp}^{3}$
options: A – II, B – I, C – III, D – IV
A – I, B – II, C – III, D – IV
A – II, B – I, C – IV, D – III
A – I, B– II, C – IV, D – III
questions.solution:
$Ni$ is in zero oxidation state in $[ Ni ( CO{)}_{4} ]$. So, the electronic configuration of $Ni$ is $3{d}^{8}4{s}^{2}$. As $CO$ is a strong ligand, it pushes all the electrons in the 3d orbital, therefore the hybridisation of $[ Ni ( CO{)}_{4} ]$ is sp3 and it has tetrahedral geometry. It is diamagnetic due to the absence of unpaired electrons.

${\left[Cu{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$ ion, oxidation state of $Cu$ is +2 and its valence shell electronic configuration is $3{d}^{9}$.  So, there would be a rearrangement of electrons in ${Cu}^{2 +}$ because of the ${NH}_{3}$ strong field ligand. And the last electron in the d-orbital would be out waiting for the N's electrons to fill up first. So, the 4 electron pairs from $N$ would be in one 3d, one 4s, & two 4p orbitals and in the third place of 4p orbital, the e- from 3d would take place. So, you can say the hybridisation here would be ${dsp}^{2}$.

${\left[Fe{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ ion, oxidation state of $Fe$ is +2 and its valence shell electronic configuration is $3{d}^{6}$. ${NH}_{3}$ is strong field ligand with complex. So, no pairing will be there. So, you can say the hybridisation here would be ${d}^{2}{sp}^{3}$.

 

${\left[Fe{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ ion, oxidation state of $Fe$ is +2 and its valence shell electronic configuration is $3{d}^{6}$. There are 4 unpaired electrons in 3d orbital.  So, you can say the hybridisation here would be ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$.

So, correct order of matching is given in the below table:

questions.solution:
d-orbital is degenerate which split into two levels ${e}_{g}$ and ${t}_{2}g$ in the presence of ligands. This splitting is due to the presence of ligands. This is called the crystal-field splitting and the energy difference between the two levels is called the crystal-field splitting energy, $\Delta0 .$

(A)  ${Ti}^{2 +}: 4{s}^{0}3{d}^{2}$

${t}_{2g}{e}^{–} = 2$
${e}_{g}{e}^{–} = 0$

${\Delta}_{0} = 2\left(- . 4{\Delta}_{0}\right) = - . 8{\Delta}_{0}$

(B)  ${V}^{2 +}: 4{s}^{0}3{d}^{3}$

${t}_{2g}{e}^{–} = 3$
${e}_{g}{e}^{–} = 0$

${\Delta}_{0} = 3\left(- . 4{\Delta}_{0}\right)$

$= - 1 . 2{\Delta}_{0}$

(C)  ${Mn}^{3 +} = 4{s}^{0}3{d}^{4}$

${t}_{2g}{e}^{–} = 3$
${e}_{g}{e}^{–} = 1$

${\Delta}_{0} = 3\left(- . 4{\Delta}_{0}\right) + 1\left(. 6{\Delta}_{0}\right)$

$= - 1 . 2{\Delta}_{0} + 0 . 6{\Delta}_{0}$

$= - 0 . 6{\Delta}_{0}$

(D)  ${Fe}^{3 +} = 4{s}^{0}3{d}^{5}$

${t}_{2g}{e}^{–} = 3$
${e}_{g}{e}^{–} = 2$

${\Delta}_{0} = 3\left(- . 4{\Delta}_{0}\right) + 2\left(. 6{\Delta}_{0}\right)$

$= - 1 . 2{\Delta}_{0} + 1 . 2{\Delta}_{0} = 0$

(p) $\left{}_{( II ) [ Cr\left(N{H}_{3}{)}_{6}\right] [ Co\left(CN{)}_{6}\right]}^{( I ) [ Co\left(N{H}_{3}{)}_{6}\right] [ Cr\left(CN{)}_{6}\right]}\right\}$ 1. Ionization
(q) $\left{}_{( IV ) [ PtB{r}_{2}\left(N{H}_{3}{)}_{4}\right]C{l}_{2}}^{( III ) [ PtC{l}_{2}\left(N{H}_{3}{)}_{4}\right]B{r}_{2}}\right\}$ 2. Hydrate

questions.solution:
Compounds (I) and (II) both contain complex cation and anion, so they show coordination isomerism.

Compounds (III) and (IV) are obtained by the interchange of groups outside the coordination sphere and the ligands within the coordination sphere. Therefore, they given different ions in the solution. Hence, they show ionization isomerism.

Compounds (V) and (VI) are linkage isomers, because the ambident ligands, SCN has two donor atoms, i.e., it has two possibilities of attachment (SCN and NCS) with the central metal. Hence, they show linkage isomerism.

Compounds (VII) and (VIII) are obtained by the replacement of a coordinated group such as $C{l}^{-}$ by water of hydration. Hence, they show hydrate isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the following
Column-I Complex Column-II
Structure / Geometry / Property
(A) ${\left[Ni{\left(CN\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 -}$ (I) Tetrahedral / Paramagnetic
(B) $\left[Ni{\left(CO\right)}_{4}\right]$ (II) Tetrahedral / Diamagnetic
(C) ${\left[{NiCl}_{4}\right]}^{2 -}$ (III) Square planar / Diamagnetic

The correct match is
questions.solution:
${\left[Ni{\left(CN\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 -}$ Square planar
The electrons are paired in $3d$ orbitals because ${CN}^{-}$ is strong field ligand.Hence the hybridisation will be ${dsp}^{2}$

$\left[Ni{\left(CO\right)}_{4}\right]$ Tetrahedral
$CO$ is strong field ligand. First the unpaired electrons will pair and then the electrons from $4s$ orbital will go in $3d$ orbital. Now $4s and 4p$ is empty hence it will be ${sp}^{3}$ hybridised.

${\left[{NiCl}_{4}\right]}^{2}$ is paramagnetic in nature due to presence of $2$ unpaired electrons.
${Ni}^{2 +}$ ion has $3{d}^{8}$ electronic configuration. It undergoes ${sp}^{3}$ hybridisation which results in tetrahedral geometry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An octahedral complex $[M(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$ has a spin-only magnetic moment of $3.87 \text{ BM}$. Which of the following correctly identifies the possible metal ion $M$ and its $d$-orbital electronic configuration?
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$.

Given $\mu = 3.87 \text{ BM}$, we have $\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 3.87$, which gives $n = 3$ unpaired electrons.

The complex is $[M(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$, so the metal ion is in the $+2$ oxidation state and the ligand ($H_2O$) is a weak field ligand.

For $V^{2+}$ ($3d^3$): The configuration in an octahedral field is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 3$.

For $Co^{2+}$ ($3d^7$): In the presence of a weak field ligand, the configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 3$.

For $Ni^{2+}$ ($3d^8$): The configuration is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 2$.

Both $V^{2+}$ and $Co^{2+}$ satisfy the condition of having 3 unpaired electrons in this weak field octahedral complex.

Answer: Both (1) and (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following coordination complexes:
(i) $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$
(ii) $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$
(iii) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$
(iv) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$
(v) $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4\right)_3\right]^{3-}$

How many of the given complexes are BOTH inner orbital AND diamagnetic?
questions.solution:
To determine if a complex is both inner orbital ($d^2sp^3$) and diamagnetic (zero unpaired electrons), we analyse the central metal ion's electronic configuration and the nature of the ligand:

(i) $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ : $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ is $3d^6$. $\mathrm{NH}_3$ acts as a strong field ligand, causing electron pairing ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$). It forms an inner orbital ($d^2sp^3$) complex and is diamagnetic. (Satisfies both)

(ii) $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ : $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ is $3d^3$. It forms an inner orbital ($d^2sp^3$) complex regardless of ligand strength ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$), but it has 3 unpaired electrons, so it is paramagnetic. (Does not satisfy both)

(iii) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$ : $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ is $3d^5$. $\mathrm{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing ($t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$). It forms an inner orbital ($d^2sp^3$) complex but has 1 unpaired electron, so it is paramagnetic. (Does not satisfy both)

(iv) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ : $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ is $3d^6$. $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs ($t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$). It forms an outer orbital ($sp^3d^2$) complex and is paramagnetic. (Does not satisfy both)

(v) $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4\right)_3\right]^{3-}$ : $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ is $3d^6$. For $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$, oxalate ($\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}$) acts as a strong field ligand, causing electron pairing ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$). It forms an inner orbital ($d^2sp^3$) complex and is diamagnetic. (Satisfies both)

Only complexes (i) and (v) are both inner orbital and diamagnetic. The total count is 2.

Answer: 2

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}$(I) Hexadentate
(B) $\mathrm{SCN}^{-}$(II) Unidentate
(C) $\mathrm{EDTA}^{4-}$(III) Ambidentate
(D) $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$(IV) Didentate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}$ (oxalate ion) coordinates through two oxygen atoms simultaneously, making it a didentate ligand.

$\mathrm{SCN}^{-}$ (thiocyanate ion) can coordinate through either the sulfur or nitrogen atom, making it an ambidentate ligand.

$\mathrm{EDTA}^{4-}$ (ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion) can bind through two nitrogen and four oxygen atoms, making it a hexadentate ligand.

$\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ coordinates through a single oxygen atom, making it a unidentate ligand.

Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.q: 1 mole of Carnallite and 1 mole of the complex $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_5\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}_2 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ are dissolved in separate flasks containing water. An excess of aqueous $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ solution is added to both flasks. What are the total moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ precipitated from the first and second flask, respectively?
questions.solution:
Carnallite is a double salt with the chemical formula $\mathrm{KCl} \cdot \mathrm{MgCl}_2 \cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. In aqueous solution, it dissociates completely into its constituent simple ions: $\mathrm{K}^+$, $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$, and $3\mathrm{Cl}^-$.

Therefore, 1 mole of Carnallite yields 3 moles of chloride ions, which will react with excess $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ to precipitate 3 moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$.

The complex $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_5\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}_2 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ contains one chloride ion inside the coordination sphere (non-ionizable) and two chloride ions outside the coordination sphere (ionizable).

In aqueous solution, 1 mole of this complex yields 2 moles of ionizable $\mathrm{Cl}^-$ ions, which will react with excess $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ to precipitate 2 moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$.

Thus, the moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ precipitated are 3 and 2, respectively.

Answer: 3 and 2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following structural conditions is strictly necessary for a coordination compound to exhibit coordination isomerism?
options: The presence of at least one ambidentate ligand in the coordination sphere
A counter ion outside the coordination sphere that can act as a potential ligand
Both the cationic and anionic entities of the salt must be complex ions
The presence of solvent molecules that can interchange with ligands in the coordination sphere
questions.solution:
Coordination isomerism occurs when there is an interchange of ligands between cationic and anionic entities of different metal ions present in a complex.

For this interchange to be possible, the coordination compound must consist of both a complex cation and a complex anion. If only one part is a complex ion and the other is a simple ion, coordination isomerism cannot occur.

The presence of an ambidentate ligand leads to linkage isomerism. A counter ion acting as a potential ligand leads to ionization isomerism. The interchange of solvent molecules leads to solvate isomerism.

Answer: Both the cationic and anionic entities of the salt must be complex ions

Assertion (A): The complexes $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{NO}_2)]\mathrm{Cl}_2$ and $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{ONO})]\mathrm{Cl}_2$ cannot be distinguished by measuring their molar conductivity in aqueous solution.
Reason (R): Linkage isomers produce the same number of ions in solution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
The complexes $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{NO}_2)]\mathrm{Cl}_2$ and $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{ONO})]\mathrm{Cl}_2$ are linkage isomers, differing only in the donor atom (N versus O) of the ambidentate ligand coordinated to the cobalt ion.

When dissolved in water, both complexes dissociate to give one complex cation and two chloride ions, producing a total of 3 ions per formula unit. Since molar conductivity depends primarily on the number of ions produced in solution, both isomers will have nearly identical molar conductivities. Therefore, they cannot be distinguished by measuring their molar conductivity.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name for the coordination complex $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5(NCS)}]\mathrm{Cl_2}$?
questions.solution:
The complex is $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5(NCS)}]\mathrm{Cl_2}$.

The complex ion is a cation $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5(NCS)}]^{2+}$, so the metal is named as cobalt.

The ligands are ammine ($\mathrm{NH_3}$) and thiocyanate ($\mathrm{NCS^-}$). According to alphabetical order, 'ammine' is named before 'thiocyanato'. There are five ammine ligands, indicated by the prefix 'penta'.

The ambidentate ligand $\mathrm{NCS^-}$ is coordinated through the nitrogen atom, which is indicated by 'thiocyanato-N' according to IUPAC conventions.

Let the oxidation state of Co be $x$. The charge on ammine is 0, thiocyanate is -1, and the complex ion has a net charge of +2 (to balance the two chloride ions).
$x + 5(0) + (-1) = +2$
$x = +3$

Combining these rules, the correct IUPAC name is Pentaamminethiocyanato-N-cobalt(III) chloride.

Answer: Pentaamminethiocyanato-N-cobalt(III) chloride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following coordination complexes is heteroleptic AND contains the central metal ion in the $+3$ oxidation state?
questions.solution:
A heteroleptic complex is one in which the central metal is bound to more than one kind of ligand.

Let us evaluate each option:
1) $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$: Contains only one type of ligand ($\mathrm{NH}_3$), so it is homoleptic. The oxidation state of Co is $+3$.
2) $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$: Contains two types of ligands ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}^-$), so it is heteroleptic. Let $x$ be the oxidation state of Cr. $x + 4(0) + 2(-1) = +1 \Rightarrow x = +3$. This satisfies both conditions.
3) $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]$: Contains two types of ligands, so it is heteroleptic. Let $x$ be the oxidation state of Pt. $x + 2(0) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +2$.
4) $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]$: Contains two types of ligands, so it is heteroleptic. Let $x$ be the oxidation state of Ni. $x + 4(0) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +2$.

Therefore, $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$ is the only complex that is both heteroleptic and has a central metal in the $+3$ oxidation state.

Answer: $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]^{+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct crystal field electronic configuration and the spin-only magnetic moment of the central metal ion in the complex $[CoF_6]^{3-}$?
questions.solution:
In the complex $[CoF_6]^{3-}$, the oxidation state of $Co$ is $+3$.

The electronic configuration of $Co$ atom is $[Ar] 3d^7 4s^2$. Therefore, the $Co^{3+}$ ion has a $3d^6$ configuration.

The complex is octahedral (coordination number $6$). According to the spectrochemical series, $F^-$ is a weak field ligand, meaning the crystal field splitting energy is less than the pairing energy ($\Delta_o < P$).

For a $d^6$ ion in a weak octahedral field, the first three electrons singly occupy the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals, the next two singly occupy the higher energy $e_g$ orbitals, and the sixth electron pairs up in one of the $t_{2g}$ orbitals.

This gives the configuration $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.

In this configuration, there are $4$ unpaired electrons ($n = 4$).

The spin-only magnetic moment is calculated as:
$\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM
$\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ BM.

Answer: $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$ and $4.90$ BM

The ligands with a higher field strength than $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ are $\text{NCS}^{-}$, $\text{edta}^{4-}$, $\text{NH}_{3}$, $\text{en}$, and $\text{CN}^{-}$.

Thus, there are 5 ligands stronger than $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$.

Answer: 5

Tetrahedral complexes are generally high-spin because the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_t$) is smaller than the pairing energy ($P$). Moreover, $Cl^-$ is a weak field ligand.

For a $d^5$ ion in a weak tetrahedral field, the electrons will fill singly into all five orbitals before pairing begins. Thus, $2$ electrons enter the $e$ orbitals and $3$ electrons enter the $t_2$ orbitals.

The correct electronic configuration is $e^2 t_2^3$.

Answer: $e^2 t_2^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): Square planar complexes of type $\text{MABCD}$ do not exhibit optical isomerism.
Reason (R): Square planar complexes possess a plane of symmetry containing the central metal atom and all four ligands.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Optical isomerism is exhibited by chiral molecules, which lack a plane of symmetry. In square planar complexes of the type $\text{MABCD}$, all four ligands and the central metal atom lie in the same plane. This molecular plane itself acts as a plane of symmetry. Since the molecule is superimposable on its mirror image, it is achiral and does not exhibit optical isomerism.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following IUPAC names represents a homoleptic complex?
questions.solution:
A homoleptic complex is one in which the central metal atom or ion is bound to only one kind of donor group (ligand).

Tris(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) sulphate contains only one type of ligand, which is ethane-1,2-diamine (a bidentate ligand). Since all the ligands attached to the cobalt ion are identical, it is a homoleptic complex.

The other options list complexes that contain more than one type of ligand (e.g., ammine along with chlorido, nitrito, or carbonato ligands). These are classified as heteroleptic complexes.

Answer: Tris(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) sulphate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A coordination compound of cobalt(III) has the empirical formula $\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4\text{NH}_3$. It is known to exhibit octahedral geometry and shows geometrical isomerism. What are the hybridization and magnetic nature of this complex?
questions.solution:
For the complex with empirical formula $\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4\text{NH}_3$ to exhibit geometrical isomerism in an octahedral geometry, it must be of the type $MA_4B_2$. This means four ammonia molecules and two chloride ions are inside the coordination sphere, giving the structural formula $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}$.

The central metal ion is $\text{Co}^{3+}$, which has an electronic configuration of $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.

For $\text{Co}^{3+}$, ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) acts as a strong field ligand. This causes the pairing of the $3d$ electrons against Hund's rule.

Since all six electrons are paired in three $3d$ orbitals, two $3d$ orbitals are left empty. These two $3d$ orbitals, along with one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals, undergo $d^2sp^3$ hybridization to form an inner orbital complex.

Because there are no unpaired electrons present in the complex, it is diamagnetic in nature.

Answer: $d^2sp^3$ and diamagnetic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following coordination complexes exhibits linkage isomerism?
questions.solution:
Linkage isomerism arises in a coordination compound containing an ambidentate ligand. An ambidentate ligand has two different donor atoms and can bind to the central metal ion through either of them.

In $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{NO}_2)]\mathrm{Cl}_2$, the $\mathrm{NO}_2^{-}$ ligand is ambidentate. It can bind through the nitrogen atom (forming a nitrito-N complex) or through an oxygen atom (forming a nitrito-O complex), thus exhibiting linkage isomerism.

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{SO}_4)]\mathrm{Br}$ contains no ambidentate ligand and instead exhibits ionization isomerism.

$[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{en})_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]$ exhibits geometrical and optical isomerism.

$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_3$ does not contain an ambidentate ligand and cannot show linkage isomerism.

Answer: $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{NO}_2)]\mathrm{Cl}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The type of isomerism exhibited by the pair of complexes $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$ and $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5(\mathrm{ONO})\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$, and the oxidation state of the central metal ion in these compounds, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
The complexes $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$ and $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5(\mathrm{ONO})\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$ differ only in the point of attachment of the ambidentate ligand $\mathrm{NO}_2^-$ (N-bound vs O-bound). This type of isomerism is called linkage isomerism.

Let the oxidation state of Co be $x$. The complex ion is $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)\right]^{2+}$.
$x + 5(0) + (-1) = +2$
$x = +3$

Thus, the isomerism is linkage isomerism and the oxidation state is $+3$.

Answer: Linkage isomerism, $+3$

(B) $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_6\right]^{3-}$(II) $\Delta_\mathrm{o} > \mathrm{P}, \mu = 0 \text{ BM}$
(C) $\left[\mathrm{Mn}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$(III) $\Delta_\mathrm{o} > \mathrm{P}, \mu = 1.73 \text{ BM}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$, $\mathrm{Fe}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3\mathrm{d}^5$). $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, so the crystal field splitting energy is greater than pairing energy ($\Delta_\mathrm{o} > \mathrm{P}$). Electrons pair up to give a $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$ configuration. It has 1 unpaired electron, so $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = 1.73 \text{ BM}$.

(B) In $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_6\right]^{3-}$, $\mathrm{Co}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3\mathrm{d}^6$). $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so $\Delta_\mathrm{o} < \mathrm{P}$. The configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$. It has 4 unpaired electrons, so $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = 4.90 \text{ BM}$.

(C) In $\left[\mathrm{Mn}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Mn}$ is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3\mathrm{d}^5$). $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand, so $\Delta_\mathrm{o} < \mathrm{P}$. The configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$. It has 5 unpaired electrons, so $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = 5.92 \text{ BM}$.

(D) In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$, $\mathrm{Co}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3\mathrm{d}^6$). $\mathrm{NH}_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$, so $\Delta_\mathrm{o} > \mathrm{P}$. The configuration is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. It has 0 unpaired electrons, so $\mu = 0 \text{ BM}$.

Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

Match the reactions given in List I with the characteristic appearance of their products in List II.

B. $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ reacts with thiocyanate ions ($\text{SCN}^{-}$) to form the $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$ complex, which gives a blood red colouration. (B-1)

C. $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ reacts with dimethylglyoxime (DMG) in a basic medium to form a rosy red (or cherry red) precipitate of bis(dimethylglyoximato)nickel(II). (C-2)

D. $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in aqueous ammonia to form the diamminesilver(I) complex, $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_{3})_{2}]^{+}$, which is a colourless solution. (D-4)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4.

Assertion (A): The complex ion $[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$ is diamagnetic in nature.
Reason (R): Oxalate ion ($C_2O_4^{2-}$) is a weak field ligand and forms a high-spin complex with $Co^{3+}$.

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of cobalt in $[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$ is $+3$. The electronic configuration of $Co^{3+}$ is $3d^6$.

Generally, oxalate ($C_2O_4^{2-}$) is a weak field ligand as it is an oxygen donor. However, with $Co^{3+}$, it acts as a strong field ligand. This is an important exception in the spectrochemical series.

Due to the strong field nature of oxalate with $Co^{3+}$, the pairing energy is less than the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o > P$). The $3d^6$ electrons pair up completely in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, giving the configuration $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.

Since there are no unpaired electrons ($n=0$), the complex is diamagnetic. Thus, the Assertion is true.

The Reason states that oxalate is a weak field ligand forming a high-spin complex with $Co^{3+}$, which is incorrect. Therefore, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Since there are no unpaired electrons ($n=0$), the complex is diamagnetic. Thus, the Assertion is true.

The Reason states that oxalate is a weak field ligand forming a high-spin complex with $Co^{3+}$, which is incorrect. Therefore, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

questions.q:
Given below are four statements regarding the geometry and magnetic property of coordination complexes:
(A) $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$ is square planar and diamagnetic.
(B) $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$ is tetrahedral and diamagnetic.
(C) $[\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-}$ is square planar and paramagnetic.
(D) $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ is octahedral and diamagnetic.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A): In $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$, Ni is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^8$). Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, pairing of electrons takes place, resulting in $dsp^2$ hybridization (square planar) and no unpaired electrons (diamagnetic). Thus, it is correct.

Statement (B): In $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$, Ni is in $0$ oxidation state ($3d^8 4s^2$). The strong field $\text{CO}$ ligand causes the $4s$ electrons to pair up in the $3d$ orbitals, giving a $3d^{10}$ configuration. This results in $sp^3$ hybridization (tetrahedral) and no unpaired electrons (diamagnetic). Thus, it is correct.

Statement (C): In $[\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-}$, Mn is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^5$). Since $\text{Br}^-$ is a weak field ligand, it forms a high-spin complex with $sp^3$ hybridization (tetrahedral) and is paramagnetic. Thus, it is incorrect.

Statement (D): In $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$, Co is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). Since $\text{F}^-$ is a weak field ligand, no pairing occurs, resulting in $sp^3d^2$ hybridization (octahedral) with four unpaired electrons (paramagnetic). Thus, it is incorrect.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The EDTA$^{4-}$ ion binds through two nitrogen and four oxygen donor atoms to a central metal ion.
Reason (R): EDTA$^{4-}$ is a hexadentate ligand.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because the structure of the ethylenediaminetetraacetate (EDTA$^{4-}$) ion contains two nitrogen atoms and four oxygen atoms (from four acetate groups) that act as donor sites.

Reason (R) is also correct because a ligand that binds through six donor atoms is termed a hexadentate ligand.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The classification of the ligand as hexadentate is a consequence of its structure, but the term 'hexadentate' itself does not explain why the specific donor atoms are two nitrogens and four oxygens (as opposed to any other combination of six donor atoms). Thus, both statements are correct, but R does not explain A.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following complex ions has the central metal ion with the crystal field electronic configuration $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$?
questions.solution:
The given electronic configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$.

Total number of d-electrons = $3 + 2 = 5$. Thus, the central metal ion must have a $d^5$ configuration.

Since the electrons have entered the higher energy $e_g$ orbitals before pairing in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, the complex must be a high-spin complex. This occurs when the crystal field splitting energy is less than the pairing energy ($\Delta_o < P$), which is characteristic of weak field ligands.

Evaluating the options:
1) $[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$: Fe is in +3 oxidation state ($d^5$). $H_2O$ is a weak field ligand, so it forms a high-spin complex with configuration $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$.
2) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$: Fe is in +3 oxidation state ($d^5$). $CN^-$ is a strong field ligand, forming a low-spin complex with configuration $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$.
3) $[Mn(CN)_6]^{4-}$: Mn is in +2 oxidation state ($d^5$). $CN^-$ is a strong field ligand, forming a low-spin complex with configuration $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$.
4) $[CoF_6]^{3-}$: Co is in +3 oxidation state ($d^6$). $F^-$ is a weak field ligand, forming a high-spin complex with configuration $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.

Therefore, $[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ matches the given configuration.

Answer: $[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following coordination complexes can exhibit linkage isomerism?
questions.solution:
Linkage isomerism arises in a coordination compound containing an ambidentate ligand. An ambidentate ligand can coordinate to the central metal ion through more than one type of donor atom.

Among the given options, the nitrite ion ($NO_2^-$) in $[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2$ is an ambidentate ligand, as it can bind through either the nitrogen atom ($-NO_2$) or the oxygen atom ($-ONO$).

The other complexes contain only unidentate ($NH_3$, $Cl^-$, $H_2O$) or bidentate ($en$) ligands that are not ambidentate. Thus, $[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2$ exhibits linkage isomerism.

Answer: $[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following coordination complexes can exhibit both linkage and ionization isomerism?
questions.solution:
Linkage isomerism arises when an ambidentate ligand (such as $\text{NO}_2^-$, $\text{SCN}^-$, or $\text{CN}^-$) is present in the coordination sphere.

Ionization isomerism occurs when a counter ion outside the coordination sphere can exchange places with a ligand inside the coordination sphere.

- $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$ exhibits only ionization isomerism (exchange of $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$).
- $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2(\text{NO}_2)\text{Cl}]$ is a neutral complex and lacks a counter ion, so it exhibits only linkage isomerism.
- $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6][\text{Cr}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$ exhibits coordination isomerism.
- $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4(\text{NO}_2)\text{Cl}]\text{Br}$ contains an ambidentate ligand ($\text{NO}_2^-$) and an exchangeable counter ion ($\text{Br}^-$ can exchange with $\text{Cl}^-$). Thus, it satisfies the structural requirements for both linkage and ionization isomerism.

Answer: $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4(\text{NO}_2)\text{Cl}]\text{Br}$

questions.q: An aqueous solution of a nickel(II) salt reacts with excess potassium cyanide to form a stable coordination complex. Which of the following correctly represents the formula, hybridization of the central metal ion, and magnetic behaviour of the resulting complex?
questions.solution:
When a nickel(II) salt reacts with excess $\text{CN}^-$, the complex formed is the tetracyanidonickelate(II) ion, $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$.

The central metal ion is $\text{Ni}^{2+}$, which has a $3\text{d}^8$ electronic configuration.

Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, it forces the pairing of the two unpaired $3\text{d}$ electrons against Hund's rule. This vacates one $3\text{d}$ orbital.

The hybridization involves one $3\text{d}$, one $4\text{s}$, and two $4\text{p}$ orbitals, resulting in $\text{dsp}^2$ hybridization (square planar geometry).

Because all electrons are paired, the complex is diamagnetic.

Answer: $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}, \text{dsp}^2, \text{diamagnetic}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The decreasing order of field strength of the given ligands is $\text{en} > \text{NH}_3 > \text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{F}^-$.
Statement II: In general, the field strength of ligands follows the order of their donor atoms: $\text{C} > \text{N} > \text{O} > \text{Halogens}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the arrangement of ligands in increasing order of their crystal field splitting energy (CFSE) is:
$\text{F}^- < \text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{en}$
Thus, the decreasing order of field strength is $\text{en} > \text{NH}_3 > \text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{F}^-$. Statement I is correct.

As a general rule, the field strength of ligands depends on the nature of the donor atom. Carbon donors (e.g., $\text{CO}$, $\text{CN}^-$) are generally stronger than nitrogen donors (e.g., $\text{en}$, $\text{NH}_3$), which are stronger than oxygen donors (e.g., $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$), and halogen donors are the weakest. Thus, the order $\text{C} > \text{N} > \text{O} > \text{Halogens}$ is correct. Statement II is also correct.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.q: Consider the geometrical isomers of the octahedral complex $[\text{Ru(H}_2\text{O})_3\text{Cl}_3]$. Which of the following statements regarding its isomers is incorrect?
options: Both the facial and meridional isomers of this complex are chiral and exhibit optical isomerism.
In the facial isomer, three identical ligands occupy adjacent positions at the corners of an octahedral face.
In the meridional isomer, three identical ligands are arranged around the meridian of the octahedron.
In the facial isomer, the bond angle between any two identical ligands is $90^{\circ}$.
questions.solution:
The complex $[\text{Ru(H}_2\text{O})_3\text{Cl}_3]$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[MA_3B_3]$, which exhibits facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism.

In the facial isomer, three identical ligands occupy adjacent positions at the corners of an octahedral face, making all bond angles between identical ligands $90^{\circ}$.

In the meridional isomer, three identical ligands are arranged around the meridian of the octahedron.

Both the facial and meridional isomers possess at least one plane of symmetry. Therefore, they are achiral (optically inactive) and do not exhibit optical isomerism.

Thus, the statement claiming they are chiral and optically active is incorrect.

Answer: Both the facial and meridional isomers of this complex are chiral and exhibit optical isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the same metal, same oxidation state and same ligands, the crystal field splitting energy in a tetrahedral complex ($\Delta_t$) is approximately $\dfrac{4}{9}$ of that in an octahedral complex ($\Delta_o$).

Reason (R): Tetrahedral complexes rarely form low-spin configurations.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is a correct statement. According to Crystal Field Theory, for the same metal ion, same oxidation state and same ligands, the relationship between tetrahedral and octahedral crystal field splitting energies is given by $\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \Delta_o$.

Reason (R) is also a correct statement. In tetrahedral complexes, the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_t$) is generally smaller than the pairing energy ($P$). As a result, electrons prefer to occupy higher energy orbitals rather than pairing up, so low-spin configurations are rarely observed.

However, Reason (R) is a consequence of the small magnitude of $\Delta_t$, not the explanation for why $\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \Delta_o$. The factor of $\dfrac{4}{9}$ arises because there are only 4 ligands instead of 6, and they do not point directly at the $d$-orbitals.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The wavelength of maximum absorption for an octahedral complex $[ML_6]^{n+}$ is $400 \text{ nm}$. The expected wavelength of maximum absorption for the corresponding tetrahedral complex $[ML_4]^{n+}$ formed by the same metal and ligands is
questions.solution:
The energy of absorption ($\Delta$) is inversely proportional to the wavelength of absorbed light ($\lambda$), as given by the Planck-Einstein relation:
$\Delta = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

The relationship between the crystal field splitting energies of tetrahedral and octahedral complexes is:
$\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \Delta_o$

Substituting $\Delta$ with $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$ gives:
$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_t} = \dfrac{4}{9} \left( \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_o} \right)$

Simplifying this relation yields:
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda_t} = \dfrac{4}{9\lambda_o}$

$\lambda_t = \dfrac{9}{4} \lambda_o$

Given that $\lambda_o = 400 \text{ nm}$, the wavelength for the tetrahedral complex is:
$\lambda_t = \dfrac{9}{4} \times 400 \text{ nm} = 900 \text{ nm}$

Answer: $900 \text{ nm}$

$\text{L}_2 = 650\text{ nm}$
$\text{L}_3 = 550\text{ nm}$

The order of wavelengths is $\text{L}_1 < \text{L}_3 < \text{L}_2$.

Therefore, the increasing order of crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) and the ligand field strength is $\text{L}_2 < \text{L}_3 < \text{L}_1$.

questions.q: Which of the following coordination complexes exhibits ionization isomerism?
questions.solution:
Ionization isomerism arises when the counter ion in a complex salt is itself a potential ligand and can displace a ligand which can then become the counter ion.

Among the given options, $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{SO}_4)]\text{Br}$ has a counter ion ($\text{Br}^-$) that can exchange with the sulfate ligand ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) inside the coordination sphere to form the ionization isomer $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$.

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms).

$[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]\text{Cl}_3$ exhibits optical isomerism due to the lack of a plane of symmetry.

$[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$ is a tetrahedral homoleptic complex that does not exhibit structural or stereoisomerism.

Answer: $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{SO}_4)]\text{Br}$

questions.q: Which of the following coordination compounds is capable of exhibiting coordination isomerism?
questions.solution:
Coordination isomerism arises from the interchange of ligands between cationic and anionic entities of different metal ions present in a complex. Therefore, the compound must contain both a complex cation and a complex anion.

Among the given options, only $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4][\mathrm{PdCl}_4]$ consists of a complex cation $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ and a complex anion $[\mathrm{PdCl}_4]^{2-}$. It can exhibit coordination isomerism (for example, forming $[\mathrm{Pd}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4][\mathrm{PtCl}_4]$).

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{NO}_2)]\mathrm{Cl}_2$ contains an ambidentate ligand and exhibits linkage isomerism.

$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]\mathrm{Cl}_3$ exhibits solvate isomerism.

$\mathrm{K}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ contains a simple cation ($\mathrm{K}^+$) and a complex anion, so it cannot show coordination isomerism.

Answer: $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4][\mathrm{PdCl}_4]$

questions.q: Which of the following complexes has a square planar geometry and exhibits geometrical isomerism?
questions.solution:
For $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$, Ni is in $0$ oxidation state ($3d^{10}$ configuration after pairing). It undergoes $sp^3$ hybridization, forming a tetrahedral geometry. Tetrahedral complexes do not show geometrical isomerism.

For $[\text{Pd}(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$, Pd is in $+2$ oxidation state. Being a 4d series element, it forms a square planar complex ($dsp^2$ hybridization). However, since ethylenediamine (en) is a symmetrical bidentate ligand, the complex is of the type $[M(AA)_2]$, which does not exhibit geometrical isomerism.

For $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$, Pt is in $+2$ oxidation state. As a 5d series element, it forms a square planar complex ($dsp^2$ hybridization). Being of the type $[Ma_2b_2]$, it exhibits cis-trans geometrical isomerism (e.g., cisplatin).

For $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$, Co is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^7$). With weak field $\text{Cl}^-$ ligands, it undergoes $sp^3$ hybridization, forming a tetrahedral geometry, which does not show geometrical isomerism.

Thus, $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ is the only complex that is both square planar and exhibits geometrical isomerism.

Answer: $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mohr's salt is a double salt and its aqueous solution gives a positive test for $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ions, whereas $\mathrm{K}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ is a coordination complex and its aqueous solution does not give a positive test for $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions.
Reason (R): In double salts, the constituent simple ions completely lose their identity in aqueous solution, while in coordination complexes, the complex ion does not dissociate into its constituent simple ions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. Mohr's salt, $\mathrm{FeSO}_4 \cdot (\mathrm{NH}_4)_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, is a double salt that dissociates completely into simple ions ($\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{NH}_4^+$, and $\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$) in aqueous solution, thus giving a positive test for $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$. On the other hand, $\mathrm{K}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ is a coordination complex that yields $\mathrm{K}^+$ and the complex ion $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}$. The complex ion does not dissociate further, so it does not give a test for $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions.

Reason (R) is not correct. According to NCERT, double salts lose their identity as a compound in solution, but their constituent simple ions retain their identity (which is why they give characteristic tests for those individual ions). The statement claims the constituent simple ions lose their identity, which is false. Coordination complexes, however, retain their identity in solution because the complex ion does not dissociate into simple ions.

Therefore, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following types of isomerism is exhibited by the coordination complex $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]$?
questions.solution:
The given complex $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[MA_3B_3]$.

Complexes of the general formula $[MA_3B_3]$ exhibit a specific type of geometrical isomerism known as facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism.

In the facial isomer, three identical ligands occupy the corners of one octahedral face. In the meridional isomer, three identical ligands occupy positions around the meridian of the octahedron.

It does not show optical isomerism because both the fac and mer isomers possess planes of symmetry. It lacks ambidentate ligands, so it cannot show linkage isomerism. Cis-trans isomerism is typically used to describe $[MA_4B_2]$ or square planar $[MA_2B_2]$ complexes.

Answer: Facial and meridional isomerism

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In aqueous solution, $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ is strongly reducing while $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ is strongly oxidising, despite both having a $d^{4}$ electronic configuration.

Reason (R): The $d^{3}$ configuration of $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ is highly stable due to a half-filled $t_{2g}$ level, whereas the $d^{5}$ configuration of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ is highly stable due to an exactly half-filled $d$-subshell.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. Both $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ have a $d^{4}$ configuration. $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ acts as a reducing agent because it gets oxidised to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$. $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ acts as an oxidising agent because it gets reduced to $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains the Assertion. In an aqueous medium, the $d^{3}$ configuration of $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ is exceptionally stable due to a half-filled $t_{2g}$ set of orbitals in an octahedral crystal field. On the other hand, $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ has a $d^{5}$ configuration, which is extra stable due to a symmetrical half-filled $d$-subshell. This difference in the stability of their product states drives their opposite redox behaviours.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Oxalate ion ($\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}$) is an example of an ambidentate ligand.
Reason (R): Oxalate ion coordinates to the central metal ion simultaneously through two oxygen atoms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
questions.solution:

Reason (R) is true because the oxalate ion has two oxygen donor atoms and it coordinates to the central metal ion simultaneously through both of these oxygen atoms to form a chelate ring.
