Assertion (A) : The complex $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ exhibits geometrical isomerism whereas $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]$ does not.
Reason (R) : Heteroleptic square planar complexes of the type $\mathrm{MA}_2\mathrm{B}_2$ can show geometrical isomerism, while homoleptic square planar complexes cannot.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false. The complex $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ is a homoleptic square planar complex (type $\mathrm{MA}_4$). In such a complex, all four coordination positions are equivalent, so it cannot exhibit geometrical isomerism. Conversely, $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]$ is a heteroleptic complex (type $\mathrm{MA}_2\mathrm{B}_2$) and it exhibits geometrical isomerism, existing as distinct cis and trans isomers.

Reason (R) is true. Geometrical isomerism arises due to different possible spatial arrangements of ligands around the central metal. This is possible in heteroleptic square planar complexes like $\mathrm{MA}_2\mathrm{B}_2$, but impossible in homoleptic square planar complexes where swapping any two identical ligands results in the same spatial arrangement.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following octahedral complexes of cobalt exhibits the highest spin-only magnetic moment?
questions.solution:
In all the given complexes, cobalt is present in the $+3$ oxidation state. The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $3\text{d}^6$.

According to the spectrochemical series, $\text{CN}^-$, $\text{en}$, and $\text{NH}_3$ act as strong field ligands for the $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ion. They cause pairing of electrons ($\Delta_o > P$), resulting in low-spin complexes with an electronic configuration of $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^6 \text{e}_{\text{g}}^0$. These complexes have $0$ unpaired electrons and are diamagnetic (spin-only magnetic moment $= 0$).

On the other hand, $\text{F}^-$ is a weak field ligand. It does not cause pairing of electrons ($\Delta_o < P$), resulting in a high-spin complex with an electronic configuration of $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^4 \text{e}_{\text{g}}^2$. This complex has $4$ unpaired electrons.

Since $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ has the maximum number of unpaired electrons, it exhibits the highest spin-only magnetic moment ($\approx 4.90 \text{ BM}$).

Answer: $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following chemical formulas represents a heteroleptic complex?
questions.solution:
Heteroleptic complexes are coordination compounds in which the central metal atom or ion is bound to more than one kind of donor group (ligand).

In $[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$, the central platinum atom is bound to two different types of ligands: ammine ($NH_3$) and chlorido ($Cl^-$). Therefore, it is a heteroleptic complex.

In $K_3[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]$, $[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3$, and $[Ni(CO)_4]$, the central metal is bound to only one type of ligand (oxalato, ammine, and carbonyl, respectively), making them homoleptic complexes. The presence of counter ions outside the square brackets (like $K^+$ or $Cl^-$) does not affect this classification.

Answer: $[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$

options: $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$ is $\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridized and diamagnetic, while $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ is $\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}^2$ hybridized and paramagnetic.

$\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$ is $\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}^2$ hybridized and paramagnetic, while $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ is $\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridized and diamagnetic.

$\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$ is $\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridized and paramagnetic, while $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ is $\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}^2$ hybridized and paramagnetic.

$\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$ is $\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridized and diamagnetic, while $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ is $\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}^2$ hybridized and diamagnetic.
questions.solution:
In both $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$ and $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$, the central metal ion is $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ which has a $3\mathrm{d}^6$ electronic configuration.

In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$, $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand. It causes pairing of the $3\mathrm{d}$ electrons against Hund's rule, leaving no unpaired electrons. Therefore, it utilizes two inner $3\mathrm{d}$ orbitals to undergo $\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridization (forming an inner orbital complex) and is diamagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$, $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand. It does not cause pairing of the $3\mathrm{d}$ electrons, leaving 4 unpaired electrons. Therefore, it utilizes outer $4\mathrm{d}$ orbitals to undergo $\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}^2$ hybridization (forming an outer orbital complex) and is paramagnetic.

Option 3 represents a common mistake where the oxidation state is miscalculated as $+3$, while Option 2 incorrectly swaps the effects of strong and weak field ligands.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$ is $\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridized and diamagnetic, while $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ is $\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}^2$ hybridized and paramagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of a transition metal ion reacts with potassium thiocyanate to produce a characteristic blood-red coloured solution. Which of the following is the formula of the coordination complex primarily responsible for this colour?
questions.solution:
The reaction between $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions and thiocyanate ions ($\text{SCN}^{-}$) produces a characteristic blood-red coloured complex.

$\text{Fe}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + \text{SCN}^{-}(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons [\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}(\text{aq})$

The blood-red colour is due to the formation of the $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$ complex (often represented with water ligands as $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})_{5}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$).

$[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})_{6}]^{3-}$ is a common misconception for the primary species formed. $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$ is the ferricyanide ion which forms Prussian blue with $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, and $[\text{Co}(\text{SCN})_{4}]^{2-}$ forms a blue complex.

Answer: $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$

questions.q: Consider the coordination compound Potassium trioxalatochromate(III). Which of the following correctly describes its ligand composition type and its optical activity?
questions.solution:
The chemical formula for Potassium trioxalatochromate(III) is $K_3[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]$.

First, analyze the ligand composition: The coordination sphere $[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$ contains only one type of ligand, which is the bidentate oxalate ion ($C_2O_4^{2-}$). Complexes with only one kind of donor group are classified as homoleptic. The presence of the counter ion (potassium) outside the coordination sphere does not make it heteroleptic.

Second, analyze the optical activity: The complex is of the type $[M(L-L)_3]^{n\pm}$, where L-L is a symmetrical bidentate ligand. Such octahedral complexes lack a plane of symmetry and are non-superimposable on their mirror images. Therefore, they exhibit optical isomerism and are optically active.

Thus, the complex is both homoleptic and optically active.

Answer: Homoleptic and optically active

(B) $[Mn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$: Mn is in +2 oxidation state. The electronic configuration is $d^5$. $H_2O$ is a weak field ligand ($\Delta_o < P$), so it forms a high-spin complex with configuration $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$. (Matches I)

(C) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$: Fe is in +3 oxidation state. The electronic configuration is $d^5$. $CN^-$ is a strong field ligand ($\Delta_o > P$), so it forms a low-spin complex with configuration $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$. (Matches IV)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Standard electrode potential)List II (Reason for the value)
(A) $E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}/\mathrm{Mn}^{2+})$(I) Positive value because high energy to transform metal to ion is not balanced by hydration enthalpy
(B) $E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}/\mathrm{Cr}^{2+})$(II) Comparatively lower positive value due to extra stability of $d^5$ configuration of $+3$ state
(C) $E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu})$(III) Negative value due to extra stability of $t_{2g}^3$ configuration of $+3$ state
(D) $E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+})$(IV) High positive value due to extra stability of $d^5$ configuration of $+2$ state

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
$E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}/\mathrm{Mn}^{2+})$ has a high positive value because the reduction of $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ ($d^4$) to $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ ($d^5$) leads to a highly stable half-filled $d$-subshell.

$E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}/\mathrm{Cr}^{2+})$ has a negative value because $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ ($t_{2g}^3$) is highly stable in aqueous solution, so $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ ($d^4$) readily oxidises to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$.

$E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu})$ is positive because the high enthalpy of atomisation and ionisation energy of copper is not balanced by its hydration enthalpy.

$E^{\circ}(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+})$ has a comparatively lower positive value than Mn because $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ($d^5$) is exceptionally stable, making its reduction to $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ($d^6$) less favourable.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An octahedral complex of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ has a spin-only magnetic moment of $0$ BM. The Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) for this complex, ignoring the pairing energy, is:
questions.solution:
The central metal ion is Fe$^{2+}$, which has an electronic configuration of $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.

The spin-only magnetic moment is given as $0$ BM. The formula for magnetic moment is $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.
Since $\mu = 0$, the number of unpaired electrons $n = 0$.

For an octahedral $d^6$ complex to have zero unpaired electrons, it must be a low-spin complex where all electrons are paired in the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals. The electronic configuration in the crystal field is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.

The Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) for an octahedral complex is calculated as:
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 n_{t_{2g}} + 0.6 n_{e_g}) \Delta_o$
where $n_{t_{2g}}$ and $n_{e_g}$ are the number of electrons in the $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals respectively.

Substituting the values:
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times 6 + 0.6 \times 0) \Delta_o$
$\text{CFSE} = -2.4 \Delta_o$

A common mistake is assuming a high-spin configuration ($t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$), which would give $-0.4 \Delta_o$, but this contradicts the given magnetic moment of $0$ BM.

Answer: $-2.4 \Delta_o$

options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Therefore, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An octahedral complex with the formula $[\text{M(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ has a spin-only magnetic moment of approximately $3.87\text{ BM}$. Identify the central metal ion $\text{M}$ from the following options:
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is given by the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu \approx 3.87\text{ BM}$, we can find $n$:
$\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 3.87$
$n(n+2) \approx 15$
This gives $n = 3$ unpaired electrons.

In the complex $[\text{M(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, the metal ion $\text{M}$ is in the $+2$ oxidation state. Since $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ acts as a weak field ligand for most $+2$ metal ions, the complex will be high-spin. We evaluate the $3d$ electron configurations for the $+2$ ions of the given options in a high-spin octahedral field:

Chromium ($\text{Cr}^{2+}$): $3d^4$. High-spin configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^1$, which has $4$ unpaired electrons.
Cobalt ($\text{Co}^{2+}$): $3d^7$. High-spin configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$, which has $3$ unpaired electrons.
Manganese ($\text{Mn}^{2+}$): $3d^5$. High-spin configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$, which has $5$ unpaired electrons.
Iron ($\text{Fe}^{2+}$): $3d^6$. High-spin configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, which has $4$ unpaired electrons.

Since $\text{Co}^{2+}$ has exactly $3$ unpaired electrons, the central metal ion $\text{M}$ is Cobalt.

Answer: Cobalt

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of coordination compounds has the same value of spin-only magnetic moment?
questions.solution:
In $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$, Co is in +3 oxidation state ($3\text{d}^{6}$). $\text{F}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so it forms a high spin complex with configuration $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$. Number of unpaired electrons ($n$) = 4.

In $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$, Fe is in +2 oxidation state ($3\text{d}^{6}$). $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand, so it forms a high spin complex with configuration $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$. Number of unpaired electrons ($n$) = 4.

Since both have $n=4$, their spin-only magnetic moment is $\sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} = 4.90 \text{ BM}$.

For other options:
$\left[\text{Mn}(\text{CN})_{6}\right]^{3-}$: $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ ($3\text{d}^{4}$), strong field ligand $\rightarrow$ $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$ ($n=2$).
$\left[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_{6}\right]^{3-}$: $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($3\text{d}^{5}$), strong field ligand $\rightarrow$ $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{5} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$ ($n=1$).
$\left[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_{4}\right]$: $\text{Ni}^{0}$ ($3\text{d}^{10}$), $n=0$.
$\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$: $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($3\text{d}^{8}$), weak field ligand $\rightarrow$ $n=2$.
$\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$: $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ($3\text{d}^{6}$), strong field ligand $\rightarrow$ $n=0$.
$\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$: $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($3\text{d}^{3}$), $n=3$.

Answer: $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ and $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of a platinum complex with the empirical formula $\text{PtCl}_4 \cdot 2\text{KCl}$ does not give a white precipitate when treated with excess $\text{AgNO}_3$. Its molar conductivity corresponds to that of a 2:1 electrolyte. What is the secondary valency of platinum in this complex?
questions.solution:
The absence of a white precipitate upon treatment with $\text{AgNO}_3$ indicates that there are no free, ionisable chloride ions in the solution. Therefore, all the chloride ions must be present inside the coordination sphere.

The complex behaves as a 2:1 electrolyte, meaning it produces a total of 3 ions per formula unit. Since the empirical formula contains two potassium atoms, these must act as the two counter cations ($\text{K}^{+}$), leaving one complex anion.

The formula of the coordination complex is $\text{K}_2[\text{PtCl}_6]$.

The secondary valency of a central metal atom is equal to its coordination number, which is the number of ligand donor atoms directly bonded to it. In $[\text{PtCl}_6]^{2-}$, platinum is bonded to 6 chloride ligands. Thus, the secondary valency of platinum is 6.

Answer: 6

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the coordination number and oxidation state of the central metal ion in the complex $[\text{Fe(EDTA)}]^{-}$?
questions.solution:
The ligand EDTA$^{4-}$ (ethylenediaminetetraacetate) is a hexadentate ligand, meaning it forms six coordinate bonds with the central metal ion. Therefore, the coordination number of iron (Fe) in $[\text{Fe(EDTA)}]^{-}$ is 6.

Let the oxidation state of Fe be $x$. The charge on the EDTA ligand is $-4$.
The sum of the oxidation states must equal the net charge of the complex ion:
$x + (-4) = -1$
$x = +3$

Thus, the coordination number is 6 and the oxidation state is +3.

Answer: 6 and +3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following coordination complexes forms an inner orbital complex?
questions.solution:
To determine whether a complex is inner or outer orbital, we examine the oxidation state, $d$-electron count, and ligand field strength:

In $[\text{Mn}(\text{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$, Mn is in the $+3$ oxidation state with a $3d^{4}$ configuration. Since $\text{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, it forces electron pairing. The electrons occupy the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, leaving two $3d$ orbitals empty. It undergoes $d^{2}sp^{3}$ hybridization, forming an inner orbital complex.

In $[\text{Ni}(\text{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{2+}$, Ni is in the $+2$ oxidation state with a $3d^{8}$ configuration. An octahedral $d^{8}$ ion cannot provide two empty $3d$ orbitals regardless of the ligand strength. Thus, it undergoes $sp^{3}d^{2}$ hybridization, forming an outer orbital complex.

In $[\text{CoF}_{6}]^{3-}$, Co is in the $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^{6}$). $\text{F}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs. It forms an outer orbital complex ($sp^{3}d^{2}$).

In $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})_{6}]^{3-}$, Fe is in the $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^{5}$). $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ acts as a weak field ligand for $\text{Fe}^{3+}$, resulting in no pairing and an outer orbital complex ($sp^{3}d^{2}$).

Answer: $[\text{Mn}(\text{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are four statements regarding coordination compounds:
(I) The complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^+$ exhibits both geometrical and optical isomerism.
(II) Facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomers are shown by octahedral complexes of type $\text{MA}_3\text{B}_3$.
(III) The complex $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$ is optically active.
(IV) Linkage isomerism arises in coordination compounds containing ambidentate ligands.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is incorrect: The complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is an octahedral complex of type $\text{MA}_4\text{B}_2$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms), but both forms possess a plane of symmetry and are optically inactive.

Statement (II) is correct: Octahedral complexes of the type $\text{MA}_3\text{B}_3$ (e.g., $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$) exhibit facial (fac) and meridional (mer) geometrical isomerism.

Statement (III) is incorrect: Platinum(II) forms square planar complexes. The complex $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$ has a square planar geometry, which contains a plane of symmetry. Hence, it is achiral and optically inactive.

Statement (IV) is correct: Linkage isomerism occurs in coordination compounds that contain ambidentate ligands (like $\text{NO}_2^-$, $\text{SCN}^-$), which can bind to the central metal atom through more than one donor atom.

Thus, only two statements (II and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An isomer of the hydrate $\text{CrCl}_3\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is dissolved in water. When one mole of this complex is treated with an excess of silver nitrate solution, two moles of a white precipitate are formed. Identify the correct structural formula of this isomer and the type of structural isomerism it illustrates when compared to the other hydrate forms.
questions.solution:
The reaction of the complex with excess $\text{AgNO}_3$ yields two moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitate per mole of the complex. This indicates that there are exactly two ionizable chloride ions present outside the coordination sphere.

Given the empirical formula $\text{CrCl}_3\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$, placing two $\text{Cl}^-$ ions outside leaves one $\text{Cl}^-$ ion and five $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecules inside the coordination sphere to satisfy the secondary valency (coordination number) of 6 for chromium.

The structural formula is therefore $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2\cdot\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Isomers that differ in the number of solvent molecules (water) directly bonded to the metal ion versus those present in the crystal lattice exhibit solvate isomerism (specifically known as hydrate isomerism when water is the solvent).

Answer: Solvate isomerism, $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2\cdot\text{H}_2\text{O}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A dark green complex has the empirical formula $\mathrm{CrCl}_3 \cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. When $1 \text{ mole}$ of this complex is treated with excess $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ solution, it yields exactly $1 \text{ mole}$ of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ precipitate. What is the structural formula of the complex, and how many water molecules are lost per formula unit when it is placed over a dehydrating agent like concentrated $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$?
questions.solution:
Precipitation of $1 \text{ mole}$ of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ per mole of the complex indicates that there is only one ionisable chloride ion present outside the coordination sphere.

To satisfy the secondary valency (coordination number) of $6$ for chromium, the remaining two chloride ions and four water molecules must be present inside the coordination sphere as ligands.

Therefore, the structural formula of the complex is $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right] \mathrm{Cl} \cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

The water molecules present outside the coordination sphere (lattice water) are easily lost when placed over a dehydrating agent like concentrated $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$. Since there are two such water molecules in the formula unit, $2$ molecules of water are lost.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right] \mathrm{Cl} \cdot 2\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} and 2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

List IList II
(A) Carnallite(I) Double salt, yields 8 ions
(B) Potash Alum(II) Complex salt, yields 5 ions
(C) $\mathrm{K}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$(III) Double salt, yields 5 ions
(D) $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]\mathrm{Cl}_4$(IV) Complex salt, yields 4 ions

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Double salts dissociate completely into simple ions in aqueous solution, whereas complex salts retain their complex ion.

(A) Carnallite is a double salt with the formula $\mathrm{KCl} \cdot \mathrm{MgCl}_2 \cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. It dissociates into $1 \mathrm{K}^+$, $1 \mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$, and $3 \mathrm{Cl}^-$, yielding a total of 5 ions. So, (A) matches with (III).

(B) Potash Alum is a double salt with the formula $\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \cdot \mathrm{Al}_2(\mathrm{SO}_4)_3 \cdot 24\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. It dissociates into $2 \mathrm{K}^+$, $2 \mathrm{Al}^{3+}$, and $4 \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$, yielding a total of 8 ions. So, (B) matches with (I).

(C) $\mathrm{K}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ is a complex salt that dissociates into $3 \mathrm{K}^+$ and $1 [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}$ ion, yielding a total of 4 ions. So, (C) matches with (IV).

(D) $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]\mathrm{Cl}_4$ is a complex salt that dissociates into $1 [\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{4+}$ and $4 \mathrm{Cl}^-$ ions, yielding a total of 5 ions. So, (D) matches with (II).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

(A) Carnallite is a double salt with the formula $\mathrm{KCl} \cdot \mathrm{MgCl}_2 \cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. It dissociates into $1 \mathrm{K}^+$, $1 \mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$, and $3 \mathrm{Cl}^-$, yielding a total of 5 ions. So, (A) matches with (III).

(B) Potash Alum is a double salt with the formula $\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \cdot \mathrm{Al}_2(\mathrm{SO}_4)_3 \cdot 24\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. It dissociates into $2 \mathrm{K}^+$, $2 \mathrm{Al}^{3+}$, and $4 \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$, yielding a total of 8 ions. So, (B) matches with (I).

(C) $\mathrm{K}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ is a complex salt that dissociates into $3 \mathrm{K}^+$ and $1 [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}$ ion, yielding a total of 4 ions. So, (C) matches with (IV).

(D) $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]\mathrm{Cl}_4$ is a complex salt that dissociates into $1 [\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{4+}$ and $4 \mathrm{Cl}^-$ ions, yielding a total of 5 ions. So, (D) matches with (II).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The complex $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$ is diamagnetic, while $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic.
Reason (R): Platinum is a 5d transition metal, and for 4d and 5d series metals, the crystal field splitting is very large, causing even weak field ligands like $\text{Cl}^-$ to force electron pairing.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
In the complex $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, the central metal ion is $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ which has a $3d^8$ electronic configuration. Since $\text{Cl}^-$ is a weak field ligand, it does not cause pairing of electrons. The complex undergoes $sp^3$ hybridization, forming a tetrahedral geometry with 2 unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic.

In the complex $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$, the central metal ion is $\text{Pt}^{2+}$ which has a $5d^8$ electronic configuration. For metals in the 4d and 5d transition series, the effective nuclear charge is higher and the d-orbitals are more spatially extended. This leads to a much larger crystal field splitting ($\Delta$) compared to the 3d series. The large $\Delta$ overcomes the pairing energy regardless of the ligand strength. Thus, even with a weak field ligand like $\text{Cl}^-$, electron pairing occurs. The complex undergoes $dsp^2$ hybridization, forming a square planar geometry with no unpaired electrons, making it diamagnetic.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Assertion (A): The ligand $\text{SCN}^-$ produces a smaller crystal field splitting ($\Delta_o$) than the ligand $\text{NCS}^-$ when forming complexes with the same metal ion.
Reason (R): In $\text{SCN}^-$, the donor atom is sulphur, whereas in $\text{NCS}^-$, the donor atom is nitrogen, which generally acts as a stronger field donor.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the ligand field strength of $\text{SCN}^-$ is less than that of $\text{NCS}^-$. Thus, $\text{SCN}^-$ produces a smaller crystal field splitting ($\Delta_o$) than $\text{NCS}^-$. Hence, Assertion (A) is true.

The ambidentate ligand thiocyanate can coordinate through either the sulphur atom ($\text{SCN}^-$) or the nitrogen atom ($\text{NCS}^-$). Nitrogen is generally a stronger field donor than sulphur, which explains why $\text{NCS}^-$ causes a larger crystal field splitting than $\text{SCN}^-$. Hence, Reason (R) is true and is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A coordination compound with the empirical formula $\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\mathrm{BrSO}_4$ exists in two isomeric forms, A and B. When an aqueous solution of form A is treated with $\mathrm{BaCl}_2$ solution, a white precipitate is formed. When an aqueous solution of form B is treated with $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ solution, a pale yellow precipitate is formed. The type of structural isomerism exhibited by forms A and B is:
questions.solution:
The formation of a white precipitate with $\mathrm{BaCl}_2$ indicates the presence of free sulphate ions ($\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$) in the solution. This means form A has sulphate outside the coordination sphere: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\mathrm{Br}\right]\mathrm{SO}_4$.

The formation of a pale yellow precipitate with $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ indicates the presence of free bromide ions ($\mathrm{Br}^-$) in the solution. This means form B has bromide outside the coordination sphere: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\mathrm{SO}_4\right]\mathrm{Br}$.

Since forms A and B differ in the distribution of ions between the coordination sphere and the ionisation sphere, they exhibit ionisation isomerism.

Answer: Ionisation isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of a $3d$ transition metal ion $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ (atomic number of $\mathrm{M} < 26$) has a spin-only magnetic moment of $4.90$ BM. Predict the redox nature of $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ in aqueous solution and the spin-only magnetic moment of the stable ion formed after its redox reaction.
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM.

Given $\mu = 4.90$ BM, the number of unpaired electrons $n = 4$.

For a $3d$ transition metal ion $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ with $Z < 26$, the ion with $4$ unpaired electrons is $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ ($3d^4$).

$\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ acts as a strong oxidising agent because it readily accepts an electron to form $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$, which has a highly stable half-filled $d^5$ configuration.

The stable product formed is $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ ($3d^5$), which has $5$ unpaired electrons.

The spin-only magnetic moment of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ is $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM.

Thus, $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ is an oxidising agent and the magnetic moment of the stable product is $5.92$ BM.

Answer: Oxidising agent; $5.92$ BM

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a hypothetical tetrahedral complex $[ML_4]^{2-}$, the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_t$) is $4000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$. The crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) for the corresponding octahedral complex $[ML_6]^{4-}$ with the same metal and ligands will be
questions.solution:
The relationship between the crystal field splitting energy of a tetrahedral complex ($\Delta_t$) and an octahedral complex ($\Delta_o$) having the same metal, the same oxidation state, and the same ligands is given by:
$\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \Delta_o$

Rearranging the formula to solve for $\Delta_o$ gives:
$\Delta_o = \dfrac{9}{4} \Delta_t$

Substituting the given value of $\Delta_t = 4000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$:
$\Delta_o = \dfrac{9}{4} \times 4000 \text{ cm}^{-1} = 9000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$

Answer: $9000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of compound X gives a positive test for $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{NH}_4^+$, and $\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions. An aqueous solution of compound Y gives a positive test for $\mathrm{K}^+$ ions but fails to give a positive test for $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{CN}^-$ ions. Identify compounds X and Y, respectively.
questions.solution:
Compound X dissociates completely in water to give tests for all its constituent ions ($\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{NH}_4^+$, and $\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$). This indicates that X is a double salt. Mohr's salt, $\mathrm{FeSO}_4 \cdot (\mathrm{NH}_4)_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, matches these constituent ions.

Compound Y gives a test for $\mathrm{K}^+$ but does not give tests for $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{CN}^-$, meaning the latter two are part of a non-ionizable coordination sphere. This indicates Y is a coordination complex containing potassium as the counter ion and iron(II) and cyanide ligands in the complex ion. Potassium ferrocyanide, $\mathrm{K}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$, matches this description.

Potassium ferricyanide is $\mathrm{K}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ which contains iron in the +3 oxidation state, not +2. Therefore, X is Mohr's salt and Y is Potassium ferrocyanide.

Answer: Mohr's salt and Potassium ferrocyanide

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The complex $[Co(en)_3]Cl_3$ is a homoleptic complex.
Reason (R): The ligand ethane-1,2-diamine coordinates to the central metal atom through two nitrogen donor atoms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because homoleptic complexes are those in which the central metal atom is bound to only one kind of donor group (ligand). In $[Co(en)_3]Cl_3$, the only ligand present inside the coordination sphere is ethane-1,2-diamine (en).

Reason (R) is also correct because ethane-1,2-diamine ($H_2NCH_2CH_2NH_2$) is a didentate ligand that binds through two nitrogen donor atoms.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The complex is homoleptic because it contains only one type of ligand, not because the ligand is didentate. A complex with a monodentate ligand can also be homoleptic (e.g., $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$).

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of a coordination compound with the empirical formula $\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 3\text{NH}_3$ does not conduct electricity and yields no precipitate upon the addition of excess $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution. Which of the following types of isomerism is exhibited by this complex?
questions.solution:
Since the aqueous solution of $\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 3\text{NH}_3$ does not conduct electricity and gives no precipitate with $\text{AgNO}_3$, there are no ionisable chloride ions outside the coordination sphere.

All three chloride ions and three ammonia molecules act as ligands to satisfy the secondary valency of cobalt (which is 6).

The formula of the complex is $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]$.

This is an octahedral complex of the type $[MA_3B_3]$. Such complexes exhibit geometrical isomerism, specifically facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism.

They do not show optical isomerism because both fac and mer isomers possess planes of symmetry.

Answer: facial and meridional isomerism

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The coordination compounds $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$ exhibit ionization isomerism.
Reason (R): Solvate isomerism arises when there is a difference in the number of solvent molecules directly bonded to the metal ion as ligands.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$ yield different ions in solution ($Br^{-}$ and $SO_4^{2-}$ respectively). This interchange of a ligand and a counter ion is the defining feature of ionization isomerism.

Reason (R) is also true as solvate (or hydrate) isomers differ in whether a solvent molecule is coordinated to the metal ion or present outside the coordination sphere in the crystal lattice.

However, Reason (R) discusses solvate isomerism, which does not explain the ionization isomerism exhibited by the complexes in Assertion (A). Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When one mole of a coordination compound with the empirical formula $\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 5\text{NH}_3$ is treated with excess aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution, two moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitate are formed. What is the correct structural formulation of this complex and its electrolyte type in aqueous solution?
questions.solution:
The formation of 2 moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitate per mole of the complex indicates that there are two ionizable chloride ions present outside the coordination sphere.

To satisfy the secondary valency (coordination number) of 6 for Cobalt(III), the remaining one chloride ion and five ammonia molecules must be present inside the coordination sphere as ligands.

Thus, the structural formula of the complex is $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$.

In aqueous solution, it dissociates as:
$[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow [\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^{-}$

Since it produces one complex cation and two chloride anions, it behaves as a 1:2 electrolyte.

Answer: $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$ and 1:2 electrolyte

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The nitrite ion ($NO_2^-$) is classified as an ambidentate ligand. Which of the following statements correctly describes the reason for this classification?
options: It possesses two different donor atoms but coordinates to the central metal ion through only one at a time.
It possesses two donor atoms and coordinates through both of them simultaneously.
It coordinates to the central metal ion in a way that forms a stable chelate ring.
It acts as a bridging ligand by coordinating to two different central metal ions simultaneously.
questions.solution:
An ambidentate ligand is a unidentate ligand that contains more than one coordinating atom but coordinates through only one donor atom at a time.

The nitrite ion ($NO_2^-$) has two potential donor atoms: nitrogen and oxygen. It can bind to a metal ion either through the nitrogen atom (forming a nitro complex) or through the oxygen atom (forming a nitrito complex), but not both simultaneously.

Coordinating through two atoms simultaneously or forming a chelate ring is characteristic of bidentate or polydentate ligands, not ambidentate ligands.

Answer: It possesses two different donor atoms but coordinates to the central metal ion through only one at a time.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following lanthanoid ions, which one acts as a strong reducing agent?
questions.solution:
The common oxidation state of all lanthanoids is $+3$.

$\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$ has an electronic configuration of $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{7}$. Despite having a stable half-filled $f$-subshell, it readily loses one electron to achieve the most common and stable $+3$ oxidation state (forming $\mathrm{Eu}^{3+}$). Therefore, it acts as a strong reducing agent.

$\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ and $\mathrm{Tb}^{4+}$ tend to gain an electron to reach the $+3$ state, making them oxidising agents. $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ is already in the stable $+3$ state with a fully filled $4f^{14}$ configuration and does not act as a reducing agent.

Answer: $\mathrm{Eu}^{2+}$

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the complex $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$, the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) is greater than the pairing energy ($P$), while for $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, $\Delta_o < P$.
Reason (R): $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$ is a low spin complex whereas $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ is a high spin complex.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
In $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$, the central metal ion is $\text{Fe}^{2+}$. Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, it causes a large crystal field splitting, making $\Delta_o > P$. This leads to the pairing of electrons in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, resulting in a low spin complex.

In $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand, causing a smaller crystal field splitting, making $\Delta_o < P$. This results in electrons occupying the $e_g$ orbitals before pairing, forming a high spin complex.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct statements. However, the spin state of the complex is a consequence of the relative magnitude of $\Delta_o$ and $P$, not the cause of it. Therefore, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:

Reason (R) is not correct. While $EDTA^{4-}$ is indeed a hexadentate ligand, it coordinates to the central metal ion through two nitrogen atoms and four oxygen atoms, not four nitrogen and two oxygen atoms.

Therefore, Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.

Statement I: The molar conductivity of $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$ in aqueous solution is greater than that of $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}$.

Statement II: The primary valency of cobalt is different in these two complexes, which causes the difference in their molar conductivities.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct because $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$ ionises to give 4 ions ($[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ and $3\text{Cl}^{-}$), whereas $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}$ ionises to give only 2 ions ($[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^{+}$ and $\text{Cl}^{-}$). A greater number of ions in solution results in higher molar conductivity.

Statement II is incorrect because the primary valency corresponds to the oxidation state of the central metal atom. In both complexes, cobalt is in the +3 oxidation state. The difference in molar conductivity is due to the number of ionisable counter ions, not a difference in primary valency.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following octahedral complexes of $\text{Ni}^{2+}$:

A: $[\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$
B: $[\text{Ni}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$
C: $[\text{Ni}(\text{en})_3]^{2+}$

The correct increasing order of the wavelength of light absorbed by these complexes is:
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the increasing order of ligand field strength is $\text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{en}$.

The crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) increases with the field strength of the ligand. A stronger field ligand produces a larger $\Delta_o$.

The energy of the absorbed light is directly proportional to $\Delta_o$ and inversely proportional to the wavelength of the absorbed light ($E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$).

Therefore, a stronger field ligand causes the absorption of light of higher energy and shorter wavelength. The increasing order of wavelength of light absorbed will be the reverse of the ligand field strength: $\text{en} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Hence, the correct order is C < B < A.

Answer: C < B < A

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the coordination complex $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ and the following statements regarding its properties:
(I) It is an inner orbital complex.
(II) Its spin-only magnetic moment is approximately $4.90 \text{ BM}$.
(III) Its crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) is $-0.4 \Delta_{\text{o}}$.
(IV) It is a diamagnetic complex.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The given complex is $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$. The central metal ion is $\text{Co}^{3+}$, which has a $3\text{d}^{6}$ electronic configuration.

Since $\text{F}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, pairing of electrons does not occur prior to filling of $\text{e}_{\text{g}}$ orbitals ($\Delta_{\text{o}} < \text{P}$). The complex is high-spin with the configuration $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4} \text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$.

Statement (I) is incorrect: It uses outer $4\text{d}$ orbitals for hybridization ($\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$), making it an outer orbital complex.

Statement (II) is correct: With 4 unpaired electrons ($n=4$), the spin-only magnetic moment is $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90 \text{ BM}$.

Statement (III) is correct: CFSE = $(-0.4 \times n_{\text{t}_{2\text{g}}} + 0.6 \times n_{\text{e}_{\text{g}}})\Delta_{\text{o}} = (-0.4 \times 4 + 0.6 \times 2)\Delta_{\text{o}} = -0.4 \Delta_{\text{o}}$.

Statement (IV) is incorrect: Due to the presence of unpaired electrons, it is a paramagnetic complex.

Thus, exactly 2 statements are correct.

Answer: 2

(iii) $\mathrm{K}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$

(v) $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_2]\mathrm{Cl}_3$

How many of the given compounds are heteroleptic complexes?
questions.solution:
A complex in which the central metal atom or ion is bound to more than one kind of donor groups (ligands) is called a heteroleptic complex. Ligands are the species present inside the coordination sphere (denoted by square brackets).

(i) $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]\mathrm{Cl}_3$ has only one type of ligand ($\mathrm{NH}_3$), so it is homoleptic. The $\mathrm{Cl}^-$ ions outside the brackets are counter ions, not ligands.
(ii) $[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]$ has two types of ligands ($\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{Cl}^-$), so it is heteroleptic.
(iii) $\mathrm{K}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ has only one type of ligand ($\mathrm{CN}^-$), so it is homoleptic.
(iv) $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4]$ has only one type of ligand ($\mathrm{CO}$), so it is homoleptic.
(v) $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_2]\mathrm{Cl}_3$ has two types of ligands ($\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$), so it is heteroleptic.

Thus, there are exactly 2 heteroleptic complexes in the given list.

Answer: 2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of coordination compounds is incorrectly matched with its type of structural isomerism?
questions.solution:
Isomers must have the identical molecular formula.

In the pair $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\mathrm{Br}\right]\mathrm{SO}_4$ and $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\mathrm{SO}_4\right]\mathrm{Cl}$, the first compound contains a bromide ion while the second contains a chloride ion. Since their molecular formulas are different, they are not isomers of each other at all, making this the incorrect match.

The other pairs are correctly matched:
$\left[\mathrm{Pt}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\right]\left[\mathrm{CuCl}_4\right]$ and $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\right]\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_4\right]$ exhibit coordination isomerism (exchange of ligands between complex cation and complex anion).

questions.q: A metal ion M (Z = 26) in +3 oxidation state forms two octahedral complexes, P and Q, with ligands $L_1$ and $L_2$ respectively. The spin-only magnetic moment of complex P is 1.73 BM and that of complex Q is 5.92 BM. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: $L_1$ is a weak field ligand and complex P has $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation
$L_2$ is a strong field ligand and complex Q has $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation
$L_2$ is a weak field ligand and complex Q has $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation
$L_1$ is a strong field ligand and complex P has $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation
questions.solution:
The metal M with atomic number 26 is Iron (Fe). In the +3 oxidation state, $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ has the electronic configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^5$.

For complex P, the spin-only magnetic moment is $\mu = 1.73$ BM. Using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$, we get $n = 1$ unpaired electron. A $3d^5$ configuration with 1 unpaired electron implies that the electrons are paired up ($t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$). This pairing occurs in the presence of a strong field ligand. Therefore, $L_1$ is a strong field ligand and complex P undergoes $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation (inner orbital complex).

For complex Q, the spin-only magnetic moment is $\mu = 5.92$ BM, which corresponds to $n = 5$ unpaired electrons. A $3d^5$ configuration with 5 unpaired electrons implies no pairing ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$). This occurs in the presence of a weak field ligand. Therefore, $L_2$ is a weak field ligand and complex Q undergoes $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation (outer orbital complex).

Hence, the statement '$L_1$ is a strong field ligand and complex P has $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation' is the only correct option.

Answer: $L_1$ is a strong field ligand and complex P has $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation

questions.q: A white precipitate $\text{X}$ is insoluble in water but dissolves readily in aqueous ammonia to form a colourless, water-soluble complex $\text{Y}$. What are the chemical formulae of $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ respectively?
questions.solution:
Among the given halides, $\text{AgCl}$ is a white precipitate, whereas $\text{AgBr}$ is pale yellow.

$\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in aqueous ammonia due to the formation of the soluble diamminesilver(I) complex. The coordination number of $\text{Ag}^+$ in this complex is 2.

The reaction is:
$\text{AgCl(s)} + 2\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)} \rightarrow [\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+\text{(aq)} + \text{Cl}^-\text{(aq)}$

Thus, $\text{X}$ is $\text{AgCl}$ and $\text{Y}$ is $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$. $\text{PbCl}_2$ does not dissolve in aqueous ammonia to form a coordination complex.

Answer: $\text{X} = \text{AgCl}, \text{Y} = [\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$ are ionisation isomers and the coordination number of cobalt in both complexes is 6.

Reason (R): Ionisation isomerism occurs when the counter ion in a complex salt is itself a potential ligand and can displace a ligand which can then become the counter ion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: The complexes $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$ yield different ions in solution ($Br^-$ and $SO_4^{2-}$ respectively), hence they are ionisation isomers. In both complexes, the central cobalt ion is bonded to 6 donor atoms (5 from $NH_3$ and 1 from $SO_4^{2-}$ or $Br^-$), making the coordination number 6.

Reason (R) is true: This is the exact definition of ionisation isomerism as per NCERT. The counter ion ($Br^-$ or $SO_4^{2-}$) acts as a potential ligand and displaces a ligand from the coordination sphere.

Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A) because it provides the underlying principle for why the given pair of complexes exhibit ionisation isomerism.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.q: What are the oxidation state and coordination number of the central metal ion in the complex $[Cr(EDTA)]^{-}$? (where EDTA is ethylenediaminetetraacetate)
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of Cr be $x$.

The ligand EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetate) carries a charge of $-4$.

The sum of oxidation states must equal the net charge on the complex ion:
$x + (-4) = -1$
$x = +3$

EDTA is a hexadentate ligand, meaning it forms 6 coordinate bonds with the central metal ion (through two nitrogen and four oxygen donor atoms).

Therefore, the coordination number of Cr in this complex is 6.

The oxidation state is +3 and the coordination number is 6.

Answer: +3 and 6

questions.q: Among the following, the species having square planar geometry for central atom are (i) $\mathrm{XeF}_4$, (ii) $\mathrm{SF}_4$, (iii) $\left[\mathrm{NiCl}_4\right]^{2-}$, (iv) $\left[\mathrm{PdCl}_4\right]^{2-}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{XeF}_4: s p^3 d^2$ hybridisation, shape is square planar instead of octahedral due to presence of two lone pair of electrons on $\mathrm{Xe}$ atom. $\mathrm{SF}_4: \mathrm{SF}_4$ molecule shows $s p^3 d$ hybridisation but its expected trigonal bipyramidal geometry gets distorted due to presence of a lone pair of electrons and it becomes distorted tetrahedral or see-saw with the bond angles equal to $89^{\circ} and 177^{\circ}$ instead of the expected angles of $90^{\circ} and 180^{\circ}$ respectively.

Experiments have, however, shown that 4coordinated complexes of $\mathrm{Pd}$ (II) are diamagnetic $(n=0)$. Thus it is $d s p^2$ hybridisation which is involved in the formation of $\left[\mathrm{PdCl}_4\right]^{2-}$ ion i.e. 4coordinated complexes of Pd(II) have square planar geometry with $n=0$ (diamagnetic).

questions.q: Which one follow 18 electron octet rule?
questions.solution:
The 18 electron rule is used for predicting the stability and rationalizing the formula, especially organomettalic complexes.
The number of valence electrons of the given species are as follows:
$\left[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CO})_5\right]-\mathrm{Mn}\left\{[\mathrm{Ar}]_{18} 3 \mathrm{~d}^5 4 \mathrm{~S}^2\right\}=7 \text{ valence }$
electrons
$\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CO})_5\right]-\operatorname{Cr}\left\{[\mathrm{Ar}]_{18} 3 \mathrm{~d}^4 4 \mathrm{~S}^2\right\}=6 \text{ valence }$
electrons
$\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CO})_5\right]-\mathrm{Fe}\left\{[\mathrm{Ar}]_{18} 3 \mathrm{~d}^6 4 \mathrm{~S}^2\right\}=8 \text{ valence }$
electrons
$\therefore\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CO})_5\right]$ follow 18 electron octet rule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many ions obtain after dissociation of this complex $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3$ ?
questions.solution:
Primary valency of coordination compounds are ionisable. Thus, dissociation of the complex, $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3$ takes place as follows $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3 \longrightarrow\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{2+}+3 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$
Therefore, total number of ions obtain will be 4 .

questions.q: In the complex, $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$, the oxidation number of Cr is
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation number of Cr is x in the complex $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+} \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \mathrm{X}+4 \times(0)+2 \times(-1) & =+1 \\ x-2 & =+1 \\ x & =+3\end{aligned}$
Thus, the oxidation number of Cr is +3 .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the reaction?
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHO}+\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{\oplus}+\mathrm{OH} \\ & \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}+\mathrm{Ag} \\ & \end{aligned}$
options: Three moles of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$are required in the above reaction
questions.solution:
Oxidation:
$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHO}+3 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}+2 \mathrm{e}^{-}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ ...(i)
Reduction:
$\left\{\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{+}+\mathrm{e}^{\ominus} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ag}+2 \mathrm{NH}_3\right\} \times 2$ ...(ii)
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHO}+\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{\oplus}+3 \mathrm{OH} \longrightarrow \\ & \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+2 \mathrm{Ag}+4 \mathrm{NH}_3 \\ & \end{aligned}$
Molecular mass of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHO}=44$
Equivalent weight $=\frac{M W}{n \text{-factor }}=\frac{44}{2}=22$
Therefore, acetaldehyde is not an oxidising agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following transition metal ions is diamagnetic?
questions.solution:
Transition metal ion having absence of unpaired electron is diamagnetic.
(1) $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^7$ (three unpaired electrons)
(2) $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^8$ (two unpaired electrons)
(3) $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^9$ (one unpaired electron)
(4) $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^{10}$ (no unpaired electron)
Thus, $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ is diamagnetic.
